docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd06 in programs/fd06_loop_pred.svh. The code consists of a short prologue, then a 16-pass outer loop starting at otop, with a 10-iteration inner loop starting at itop, and a short epilogue.

The inner loop's branch I at 0x8000_0016 returns to itop. The outer loop's branch O at 0x8000_0020 returns to otop.

The program runs in machine mode with translation off, so the addresses are physical. The program starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv).

                                                              Position from
Address      Label   Instruction          Purpose              otop   itop
0x8000_0000          c.addi a0, 1         ; prologue
0x8000_0002          addi   t0, t0, 1     ; prologue
0x8000_0006          c.addi a0, 1         ; prologue

0x8000_0008  otop:   c.addi a0, 1         ; filler                0
0x8000_000A          addi   t0, t0, 1     ; filler                1
0x8000_000E  itop:   c.addi a0, 1         ; filler                3      0
0x8000_0010          addi   t0, t0, 1     ; filler                4      1
0x8000_0014          c.addi a0, 1         ; filler                6      3
0x8000_0016  I:      bne    x6, x0, itop  ; inner loop branch     7      4
0x8000_001A          c.addi a0, 1         ; filler                9      6
0x8000_001C          addi   t0, t0, 1     ; filler               10      7
0x8000_0020  O:      bne    x6, x0, otop  ; outer loop branch    12      9

0x8000_0024          c.addi a0, 1         ; epilogue
0x8000_0026          addi   t0, t0, 1     ; epilogue
0x8000_002A          c.addi a0, 1         ; epilogue
0x8000_002C  hold:   jal    x0, hold      ; termination

A position is the halfword offset of an instruction from the start of its prediction block. The 32-bit instructions take two positions.

With one prediction slot, an FTB entry holds one branch, so the loops are predicted as several blocks. The accepted p2 slot groups, by block:

Block start Reached by Branch Position Block end Groups 0x8000_0008 (otop) O taken I 7 0x8000_0028 15 0x8000_000E (itop) I taken I 4 0x8000_002E before the split 55 0x8000_000E (itop) I taken I 4 0x8000_0020 after the split 105 0x8000_001A I corrected to not taken O 3 0x8000_003A 3 0x8000_0020 (O) The block at itop ending at O O 0 0x8000_0040 10

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the branches.

The direction of each branch is chosen by the program writer class and resolved by the modeled backend. The register operands play no part in the taken/not taken state. The code is the same on every pass, and only the expected instruction stream changes.

I is taken 9 times and not taken once per pass, which gives 16 exits with the same trip count. O is taken on passes 0 to 14 and falls through on pass 15 (event 13).

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text: Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

docs.title: 4.1 Predicting the inner exit
docs.text:
The loop predictor allocates an entry when an update misses on a taken backward branch, so I's first taken resolution allocates one, at cyc 20.1 An exit at a known count trains the entry. A count equal to the learned trip count, past_itr, raises the confidence cnf by one, and any other count clears cnf and learns the count. A taken resolution at or past the learned count clears cnf.2

The LP predicts only at full confidence, 3. It then predicts taken while the speculative count is below the trip count, so the exit is predicted not taken.3 At p1, a trusted LP overrides the direction of a slot the uBTB supplied.4 At p2, it takes priority over TAGE.5 The slot carries pred_src PRED_LOOP in both cases.

Each of the 16 exits retires with a final slot from one of three predictors, the last group the FTQ accepted for its entry.

passes   final slot from   direction   result
0 to 3   TAGE              taken       mispredicted; the backend redirects
4 to 7   SC                not taken   correct
8 to 15  loop predictor    not taken   correct

The exits and the LP's training across the run are shown below.

The exits of passes 0 to 3 are the backend redirects to 0x8000_001A, from cyc 49 (event 2) to cyc 140 (event 4). The LP is still training over this time: lp_past_itr first reads 8 at cyc 116 (event 3), and lp_conf first reads 1 at cyc 140 and 2 at cyc 199.

The learned count is 8, not 9 or 10, because the LP indexes its table by the request PC, the start of the prediction block, and not by I's PC. The first iteration of each pass predicts I in the block at otop, which has its own LP entry. The other nine predict it in the block at itop, so that entry sees 8 taken branches and then the exit, at lp_curs 8.6

In passes 4 to 7, TAGE still predicts I taken at the exit, and SC reverses it at p3. The first reversal is at cyc 162 (event 5) and the last at cyc 238 (event 7). The first redirects to 0x8000_002E, the end of the block at itop. The FTB update at cyc 173 (event 6) ends that entry at O's PC, so the other three redirect to 0x8000_0020.

lp_conf reaches 3 at cyc 248 (event 8), and the LP supplies I's direction from cyc 256 at p1 (event 9) and cyc 257 at p2 (event 10). It first predicts an exit at cyc 259 (event 11), and the monitor counts the first such exit at retirement at cyc 266 (event 12), in pass 8. Every exit from there on comes from the LP.

The backend reports 11 mispredictions in the run. Besides the four exits, three are I taken, at cyc 21, 31 and 69, three are O taken, at cyc 59, 171 and 196, and one is O falling through at cyc 429 (event 13).

docs.title: 4.2 The loop predictor taking over
docs.text:
The waveform group loop_pred_p1_p2 shows the LP's answers for the block at p1 and p2, not the table entry. The p2 answer describes I only in the cycles its block is at p2, and reads 0 otherwise.

At cyc 116 (event 3), u_bpu.w_lp_pred_p2.[0].lp_past_itr first reads 8, while bpu_slot_p2.[0] is still PRED_TAGE. At cyc 248 (event 8), lp_conf first reads 3.

At cyc 256 (event 9), u_bpu.w_lp_pred_p1.[0].lp_pred_is_loop is asserted and bpu_pred_slot_p1.[0].pred_src is PRED_LOOP, with u_ftq.w_ok_pred_p1 asserted. At cyc 257 (event 10), u_bpu.w_lp_pred_p2.[0].lp_pred_is_loop is asserted and bpu_slot_p2.[0].pred_src is PRED_LOOP.

At cyc 259 (event 11), the speculative count lp_curs reads 8, equal to lp_past_itr. lp_pred_taken is deasserted, and bpu_slot_p2.[0] holds I at pos 4 with taken deasserted and pred_src PRED_LOOP.

docs.title: fd07_calls_returns: Calls and Returns
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd07_calls_returns (FD-7) runs a loop of 8 passes. Each pass makes nested calls, then a recursion four calls deep from one call site, then a coroutine switch by two return-calls.

The return address stack (RAS) pushes a call's return address and pops it for a return at p2, which supplies the return's target. A recursive call whose return address matches the top of the stack increments that entry's count, spec_rctr, instead of allocating an entry. A return-call pops and then pushes in one operation.

The RAS supplies the target of 64 of the 80 retired returns and return-calls. The result line in the log file reports that count, the p2 operations, and the highest recursion count.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd07 in programs/fd07_calls_returns.svh. The code consists of a short prologue, then a loop of 8 passes starting at top, and a short epilogue.

Each pass calls f1, which calls f2. It then calls f, which calls itself four times from the one call site at 0x8000_080A. It then calls B through x5, and B and the main code switch by the return-calls B1 and A1. B returns through x5 at B2, and the back edge at 0x8000_002A returns to top.

The program runs in machine mode with translation off, so the addresses are physical. The program starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv).

Address      Label  Instruction             Purpose               Block  Pos
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue

0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1            ; filler              008    0
0x8000_000A         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler              008    1
0x8000_000E         jal    x1, f1           ; call                008    3
0x8000_0012         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler              012    0
0x8000_0014         jal    x1, f            ; call                012    1
0x8000_0018         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler              018    0
0x8000_001A  L:     jal    x5, B            ; call through x5     018    1
0x8000_001E         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler              01E    0
0x8000_0020         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler              01E    1
0x8000_0024  A1:    jalr   x5, 0(x1)        ; return-call         01E    3
0x8000_0028         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler              028    0
0x8000_002A         bne    x6, x0, top      ; back edge           028    1

0x8000_002E         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_0030         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8000_0034         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_0036  hold:  jal    x0, hold         ; termination

0x8000_0500  f1:    c.addi a0, 1            ; filler              500    0
0x8000_0502         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler              500    1
0x8000_0506         jal    x1, f2           ; nested call         500    3
0x8000_050A         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler              50A    0
0x8000_050C         ret                     ; return to main      50A    1

0x8000_0600  f2:    c.addi a0, 1            ; filler              600    0
0x8000_0602         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler              600    1
0x8000_0606         ret                     ; return to f1        600    3

0x8000_0800  f:     c.addi a0, 1            ; filler              800    0
0x8000_0802         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler              800    1
0x8000_0806         bne    x6, x0, f+16     ; taken at the bottom 800    3
0x8000_080A         jal    x1, f            ; recursive call      80A    0
0x8000_080E         c.addi a0, 1            ; after a return      80E    0
0x8000_0810         ret                     ; return from f       80E    1

0x8000_0A00  B:     c.addi a0, 1            ; filler              A00    0
0x8000_0A02         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler              A00    1
0x8000_0A06  B1:    jalr   x1, 0(x5)        ; return-call         A00    3
0x8000_0A0A         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler              A0A    0
0x8000_0A0C         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler              A0A    1
0x8000_0A10  B2:    jalr   x0, 0(x5)        ; return              A0A    3

Block is the low bits of the start address of the prediction block that holds the instruction, and Pos is its halfword position from that start. With one prediction slot, each block holds one branch. The ret at 0x8000_0810 is also predicted in a block of its own at 0x8000_0810, position 0, when the branch at 0x8000_0806 is taken.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the branches.

The program writer types each branch from its link registers, x1 and x5. A jal with a link register as rd is a DIRECT_CALL. A jalr with a link register as rs1 and not as rd is a RETURN, and one with unequal link registers as rd and rs1 is a RETURN_CALL. The directions and targets are chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in them.

Each pass retires 8 direct calls, 8 returns and 2 return-calls. The 8 returns are f2's, f1's, 5 from f and B2. Over 8 passes that gives 80 retired returns and return-calls, the total the monitor's count is out of.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text: Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

docs.title: 4.1 Predicting the returns
docs.text:
The RAS holds two stacks. The speculative stack has 16 entries and changes at p2, and it is empty when TOSR equals BOS. The commit stack has 32 entries, changes as calls and returns retire, and holds one entry per call with no count.1

A slot of the p2 group goes to the RAS when it holds a branch of a valid block and no earlier slot of the block is taken.2 A call pushes its fall-through address. If that address equals the top entry's, the entry's spec_rctr is incremented and the pointers do not move. Otherwise a new entry is allocated at TOSW.3 A return pops: a non-zero count is decremented and TOSR holds, and a count of 0 sends TOSR to the entry below.4 A RETURN_CALL pops and then pushes.5 The pop supplies the slot's target with pred_src PRED_RAS at p2, and a return slot from the uBTB takes the top of the stack at p1.6

A commit moves BOS to the TOSR its block left.7 A pop of an empty speculative stack reads the top of the commit stack and changes neither stack.8 A backend redirect restores TOSR, TOSW and BOS from a snapshot and leaves the entries and their counts as they are.9

The monitor's count of 64 divides across the passes as follows.

pass     returns   from the RAS   not from the RAS
0        10        2              7 not yet in the FTB; f's last return
1        10        8              f1's return; f's last return
2 to 7   10 each   9 each         f's last return

In pass 0, no return reaches p2 before cyc 162 (event 7), and the backend corrects each return the FTB does not hold yet. In pass 1, f1's return at cyc 248 finds both stacks empty, so it takes the FTB's target with pred_src PRED_FTB.

F's last return is mispredicted in all 8 passes, for one reason. The recursive call at 0x8000_080A pushes 0x8000_080E each time. The first allocates an entry and the other three increment it, so the blocks of all four calls leave TOSR on that entry. When the first of them commits, BOS moves to the entry, and the speculative stack is empty.

Pass 6 shows the sequence. Entry 9 is allocated at cyc 578, and its count reaches 3 at cyc 589. The first recursive call commits at cyc 588, which moves BOS to 9. The returns reach p2 from cyc 594 with the stack empty, so each takes the top of the commit stack, 0x8000_080E, and the count of entry 9 stays at 3. The first four returns are correct. The fifth returns to main at 0x8000_0018, but no return has committed yet, so the top still reads 0x8000_080E. The backend corrects it at cyc 606. The figure below shows these cycles.

The redirect to 0x8000_0018 is at cyc 172 in pass 0 (event 9), at cyc 294, 361, 427, 494, 550 and 606 in passes 1 to 6, and at cyc 662 in pass 7 (event 15).

The other returns come from the speculative stack, where the calls are recent enough that the stack is not empty. The first is f2's in pass 1 at cyc 246 (event 10), which pops 0x8000_050A with TOSR at 2 and BOS at 1.

The recursion count differs by pass.

pass   entry    highest count   count rises at cyc
0      1        4               131 to 137
1      4        4               267 to 273
2      11, 12   1               325, 341
3      3        3               392 to 400
4      10, 11   1               458, 474
5      2        3               525 to 533
6      9        3               581 to 589
7      0        3               637 to 645

Four recursive calls give a count of 3. The count of 4 in passes 0 and 1 comes from a fifth call on a predicted path. At the bottom of the recursion the branch at 0x8000_0806 is predicted not taken, so the path calls f again and the count reaches 4 at cyc 137 (event 4). The backend redirects to 0x8000_0810 at cyc 139 (event 5). The redirect does not change the count, so entry 1 holds 4 until the entry is reallocated at cyc 374 (event 14). Pass 3 also makes a fifth call, at cyc 404, but the stack is empty by then, so that call allocates an entry and the count stays at 3.

In passes 2 and 4, a p3 redirect sends the path to 0x8000_0810 after the second recursive call, at cyc 327 and 460. A pop then decrements the count, the first at cyc 330 (event 13), and the backend redirects to 0x8000_080A at cyc 335 and 468. The recursion continues in a new entry. The pops at cyc 330, 343, 463 and 476 are the only ones in the run that decrement a count.

The first return-calls at p2 are on a predicted path that is later redirected. The p3 redirect at cyc 252 leads to B1 at cyc 256 (event 11), and the backend redirect at cyc 261 removes it. The return-calls of the retired path first reach p2 in pass 1. At cyc 298 (event 12), B1 pops 0x8000_001E and pushes 0x8000_0A0A. At cyc 300, A1 pops 0x8000_0A0A and pushes 0x8000_0028. At cyc 302, B2 pops 0x8000_0028.

The backend reports 25 mispredictions in the run: 12 in pass 0, 3 in pass 1, 2 each in passes 2, 3 and 4, 1 each in passes 5 and 6, and 2 in pass 7. The single redirects of passes 5 and 6 are f's last return. Pass 7 adds the back edge falling through at cyc 683 (event 16).

docs.title: 4.2 The stack operations in the waveform
docs.text:
The waveform group ras shows the pointers, the entries and the p2 operation. bpu_slot_p2.[0].target is the address the pop supplies.

At cyc 128 (event 2), u_bpu.w_ras_pred_val_p2.[0] is asserted with u_bpu.w_br_type_p2.[0] DIRECT_CALL and u_bpu.r_pc_p2 at 0x8000_080A. By cyc 130, u_ras.tosr reads 1 and u_ras.tosw reads 2. u_ras.spec_rctr.[1] reads 1 at cyc 131 (event 3) and steps to 4 at cyc 137 (event 4), while tosr holds.

At cyc 162 (event 7), tosr and bos both read 1 and u_ras.p2_pre_empty.[0] is asserted. bpu_slot_p2.[0].target is 0x8000_080E with pred_src PRED_RAS, the value of u_ras.commit_top_addr in the ras_commit group.

At cyc 246 (event 10), tosr reads 2 and bos reads 1, and p2_pre_empty.[0] is deasserted. The target is 0x8000_050A, the value of u_ras.spec_ret_addr.[2].

At cyc 298 (event 12), w_br_type_p2.[0] is RETURN_CALL at r_pc_p2 0x8000_0A00, and tosr and tosw read 5 and 6. They read 6 and 7 at cyc 300, so the pop and the push of the one operation show as one step.

From cyc 594 to cyc 601, in pass 6, tosr and bos both read 9, p2_pre_empty.[0] is asserted on each pop, spec_rctr.[9] holds 3, and commit_top_addr holds 0x8000_080E. The backend's redirect to 0x8000_0018 is at cyc 606, in the backend group.

docs.title: fd08_indirect: Indirect Jump
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd08_indirect (FD-8) runs a loop of 40 passes. Each pass runs an indirect jump, J, and an indirect call, K, whose targets alternate from pass to pass. Each follows a conditional, A and C, whose direction alternates with it, so the global history differs between odd and even passes.

An FTB entry holds one target for its jump, so it cannot follow a target that changes every pass. ITTAGE learns each target under its history and supplies it at p2, and the slot's pred_src is PRED_ITTAGE.

ITTAGE supplies the correct target of 50 of the 80 retired executions of J and K. The result line in the log file reports that count.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

docs.title: 1.1 Files
docs.text:
DEMO=$RVA_ROOT/examples/fe_demo

File Path This file $DEMO/docs/fd08_indirect.md Program (stimulus) $DEMO/programs/fd08_indirect.svh Surfer sucl $DEMO/waves/fd08_indirect.sucl Log $DEMO/out/fd08_indirect/fd08_indirect.log Waveform $DEMO/out/fd08_indirect/fd08_indirect.fst Waveform (online) Link Block connectivity $DEMO/docs/fe_block.svg Pipeline view $DEMO/docs/fe_pipe.svg Common description $DEMO/docs/demo_explainer.md

docs.title: 2. Run the scenario
docs.text:
Run simulation: 

make -C examples/fe_demo fd08_indirect

View the waveform (runs simulation first if FST is not up to date): 

make -C examples/fe_demo view S=fd08_indirect

Console output: 

-I: fd08_indirect : PASS : cyc = 1147

Log file output: 

-I: fd08_indirect: PASS, indirect targets predicted by ITTAGE 50,
    events checked 16 of 16, cyc 1147

The testbench monitor, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh, supplies the count in the log line:

  • indirect targets predicted by ITTAGE
    • n_itt_ok in tb/fe_demo_mon.svh
    • retired INDIRECT_NONRET or INDIRECT_CALL whose final slot in the FTQ entry has pred_src PRED_ITTAGE, taken 1 and the correct target

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd08 in programs/fd08_indirect.svh. The code consists of a short prologue, then a loop of 40 passes starting at top, and a short epilogue.

The conditional A at 0x8000_000A is taken on odd passes and skips one instruction. The jump J at 0x8000_0010 goes to ta on odd passes and tb on even passes, and both lead to jn. The conditional C at 0x8000_0502 is taken on even passes. The call K at 0x8000_0508 goes to fa on odd passes and fb on even passes. The branch X at 0x8000_050E is taken only on the last pass, and exits the loop.

The program runs in machine mode with translation off, so the addresses are physical. The program starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv).

Address      Label  Instruction             Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue

0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8000_000A  A:     bne    x6, x0, 0x010    ; taken on odd passes
0x8000_000E         c.addi a0, 1            ; even passes only
0x8000_0010  J:     jalr   x0, 0(x7)        ; indirect jump, to ta or tb

0x8000_0400  ta:    c.addi a0, 1            ; odd passes
0x8000_0402         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; odd passes
0x8000_0406         jal    x0, jn           ; odd passes

0x8000_0480  tb:    c.addi a0, 1            ; even passes
0x8000_0482         jal    x0, jn           ; even passes

0x8000_0500  jn:    c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8000_0502  C:     bne    x6, x0, 0x508    ; taken on even passes
0x8000_0506         c.addi a0, 1            ; odd passes only
0x8000_0508  K:     jalr   x1, 0(x28)       ; indirect call, to fa or fb
0x8000_050C         c.addi a0, 1            ; after the return
0x8000_050E  X:     bne    x6, x0, 0x516    ; taken on the last pass
0x8000_0512         jal    x0, top          ; back edge

0x8000_0516         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_0518         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8000_051C         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_051E  hold:  jal    x0, hold         ; termination

0x8000_0600  fa:    c.addi a0, 1            ; odd passes
0x8000_0602         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; odd passes
0x8000_0606         ret                     ; odd passes

0x8000_0680  fb:    c.addi a0, 1            ; even passes
0x8000_0682         ret                     ; even passes

J is an INDIRECT_NONRET because neither register is a link register, and K is an INDIRECT_CALL because rd is x1. The ret in fa and fb is a RETURN, predicted by the RAS.

With one prediction slot, an FTB entry holds one branch, so the path to J and K is predicted as several blocks. The accepted p2 slot groups, by block:

Block start Reached by Branch Position Block end Groups 0x8000_0008 top A 1 0x8000_0028 before the split 6 0x8000_0008 top A 1 0x8000_0010 after the split 51 0x8000_000E a backend redirect, A not taken J 1 0x8000_0014 11 0x8000_0010 A taken, or the block at 0x8000_0008 ends J 0 0x8000_0014 59 0x8000_0500 jn C 1 0x8000_0520 before the split 5 0x8000_0500 jn C 1 0x8000_0508 after the split 66 0x8000_0506 a backend redirect, C not taken K 1 0x8000_050C 6 0x8000_0508 C taken, or the block at 0x8000_0500 ends K 0 0x8000_050C 63

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the branches.

The directions and targets are chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in them. The jalr encodings are the same on every pass, and x7 and x28 are never read. The code is the same on every pass, and only the expected instruction stream changes.

J and K each retire 40 times, 20 times to each of their two targets, which gives the 80 retired executions in the count.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text: Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

docs.title: 4.1 Predicting the indirect targets
docs.text:
An FTB entry holds one jump target, written when the jump resolves.1 ITTAGE reads its tables with the request PC, the start of the prediction block, and the folded global history.2 On a tagged hit at p2, the slot takes the ITTAGE target and pred_src PRED_ITTAGE. Without a hit it takes the FTB target and PRED_FTB.3 A misprediction writes the provider's target when its counter is 0, and allocates in a higher table when a candidate exists.4

Each of the 80 executions retires in one of three ways.

passes     ITTAGE, correct   FTB, correct   backend redirect
0 to 7     3                 6              7
8 to 19    22                0              2
20 to 25   2                 0              10
26 to 39   23                0              5
total      50                6              24

The figure below shows each execution by pass.

In passes 0 to 7, the entries are being built. The first allocation is for K at cyc 60 (event 2). The first tagged hit and the first target of K from ITTAGE are at cyc 260 (events 4 and 5), and the first target of J from ITTAGE is at cyc 267 (event 6). The monitor counts the first at retirement at cyc 267 (event 7). The 6 correct targets from the FTB are the executions where the target the entry holds matches the pass.

The FTB splits the blocks at 0x8000_0500 and 0x8000_0008 at cyc 229 and cyc 298 (events 3 and 8), so that they end at K and J. From then on, a correct prediction of A or C leads to the block starting at J or K on both odd and even passes, and that block's FTB entry holds one target. A conditional predicted taken and resolved not taken instead redirects to 0x8000_000E or 0x8000_0506, a different block with its own ITTAGE entries.

In passes 8 to 19, J is correct in every pass. A is predicted taken in the even passes, and the backend redirects to 0x8000_000E at cyc 345, 392, 445, 492, 530 and 568. J is then predicted in the block at 0x8000_000E, whose entry holds tb. In odd passes it is predicted in the block at 0x8000_0010, whose entry holds ta.

K has the two redirects of these passes. In pass 9, table 1 answers fb on an odd pass, and the backend redirects to fa. The update allocates in table 2 at cyc 378 (event 9). Pass 13 also redirects to fa and allocates in table 3 at cyc 478, and K's target first comes from table 3 at cyc 517. ITTAGE also corrects the p1 prediction from cyc 398 (event 10), the first of 30 p2 redirects on an indirect slot.

In pass 20, A is predicted correctly on an even pass for the first time since pass 6, so J is predicted in the block at 0x8000_0010. Table 1 answers ta there, and the backend redirects to tb at cyc 607 (event 11). J is redirected 4 times and K 6 times in passes 20 to 25, while new entries are allocated in tables 1 to 3. J first takes tb from table 2 in that block at cyc 780 (event 12), in pass 26.

From pass 26 to pass 39, ITTAGE supplies 23 of the 28 targets. The last indirect redirect is K in pass 36, at cyc 1056 (event 13). The loop exits in pass 39 at cyc 1137 (event 14).

docs.title: 4.2 The ITTAGE answers in the waveform
docs.text:
The waveform group ittage_p2 shows ITTAGE's answer for the block at p2, with u_bpu.w_ftb_jmp_target_p2, the FTB's target, beside it. ittage_prm_tgt and ittage_alt_tgt hold VA[40:1], so each reads half of the target address.

At cyc 260 (events 4 and 5), ittage_hit is asserted with ittage_prm_comp 1. bpu_slot_p2.[0] holds K at pos 0 with target 0x8000_0680 and pred_src PRED_ITTAGE. w_ftb_jmp_target_p2 reads the same address.

docs.title: fd09_tage: TAGE Provider, Allocation and use_alt_on_na
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
Scenario fd09_tage (FD09) shows three behaviors of the Pacino TAGE predictor in response to fetch target queue (FTQ) prediction requests at pipestage p0 and FTQ updates at pipestage u0:

  1. a prediction supplied by a tagged table
  2. the allocation of a new tagged entry after a misprediction
  3. the use_alt_on_na1 mechanism handing a prediction from a weak tagged entry to the base table T0.

FD09 runs a loop whose body contains a conditional branch with a random direction. The random direction is chosen by the program writer class and resolved by the modeled backend. With the random direction the predictor cannot learn the branch behavior and therefore mispredicts often. These mispredictions result in allocations and eventually trigger the use_alt_on_na (UAON) counter. Eventually the UAON counter causes the prediction to use the base table T0 as the prediction source.

Branch predictors and decoupled frontend designs are well-researched. Some of the seminal papers include [1] [2] [3] [4].

Pacino terminology labels the prediction operation stages as p0/p1/etc and the branch predictor update operation stages u0/u1/etc.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1, to reduce the volume of signal data.

The testbench monitor, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh, supplies the counts in the log line:

  • tagged-provider predictions
    • n_tage_prov in tb/fe_demo_mon.svh

  • allocations

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd09 in programs/fd09_tage.svh. The code consists of a short prologue, then a 256 iteration loop, and a short epilogue.

The loop body holds two conditional branches. The bne branch at 0x8000_000E has a randomized direction. The bne branch at 0x8000_0016 returns to label top. This is the loop's back edge, labeled BE in the listing below.

The program runs in machine mode with translation off, so the addresses are physical. The program starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv), and the loop's first instruction, top, is at 0x8000_0008.

                                                         Position in fetch block
Address      Label  Instruction          Purpose         top   ft  dest   BE
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1         ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1     ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1         ; prologue

0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1         ; loop body       0
0x8000_000A         addi   t0, t0, 1     ; loop body       1
0x8000_000E  B:     bne    x6, x0, dest  ; random          3
0x8000_0012  ft:    c.addi a0, 1         ; B not taken     5    0
0x8000_0014  dest:  c.addi a0, 1         ; loop body       6    1     0
0x8000_0016  BE:    bne    x6, x0, top   ; back edge      (7)   2     1    0

0x8000_001A         c.addi a0, 1         ; epilogue
0x8000_001C         addi   t0, t0, 1     ; epilogue
0x8000_0020         c.addi a0, 1         ; epilogue
0x8000_0022  hold:  jal    x0, hold      ; termination

A position is the halfword offset of an instruction from the start of its fetch block. The 32-bit instructions take two positions, so the addi at 0x8000_000A covers 1 and 2. The block at top ends at BE once the FTB has split its entry (section 4.2), so BE is at position 7 only before the split. After it, BE is in a fetch block of its own: position 0 at BE, 1 at dest (B taken) and 2 at ft (B resolved not taken). The figure in section 4.2 shows the fetch blocks.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to keep both branches away from the start of the fetch block at top: B is at position 3 of that block and BE at position 7.

Since B's direction is randomized the predictor cannot predict its direction. Therefore the bne at B mispredicts often. The mispredictions cause TAGE table entry allocations and train the use_alt_on_na counter.

The direction of each occurrence of B is chosen by the program writer class and resolved by the modeled backend. The register operands play no part in the taken/not taken state.

B is taken on roughly 1 in 8 iterations, 33 of 256 in the simulation. From 0, the first taken iterations are 9, 16, 19, 22, 30 and 31. RISC-V has no branch delay slots: when B is taken, the c.addi at 0x8000_0012 is skipped.

The back edge is taken on iterations 0 to 254 and falls through on iteration 255. Its pattern is regular, and the predictors learn it.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text: Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

docs.title: 4.1 TAGE structure
docs.text:
Pacino's TAGE implementation uses 5 tables, T0-T4. T0 is the base predictor which is untagged. T1 to T4 are tagged and use direction history in their access address generation and entry matching. The tagged tables use an increasing number of history bits (length), 8, 13, 32 and 119, respectively.

T0 holds a 2-bit counter per entry and always produces a prediction.

A tagged table produces a prediction only when its tag matches. Each tagged entry holds a 3-bit prediction counter, CTR, which encodes a predicted direction in its MSB and a confidence value in the lower bits.

The format for entries in tables T1 to T4 is shown below. All four use the same 8-bit tag.4

For the tagged tables, two predictions are possible, a 'primary' and an 'alternative' prediction. The table with the longest history that matches the tag produces the primary prediction, and the next longest matching table is the alternative prediction or T0 when no other tagged table matches.

A prediction moves through four stages, p0 to p3. The FTQ presents the request at p0, TAGE reads its tables at p1 and delivers its prediction at p2. TAGE's first p2 response is at cyc 2. In all the scenarios the statistical corrector (SC) is enabled. SC takes the TAGE p2 output and uses one cycle to deliver its prediction at p3. If the SC prediction is different from the TAGE prediction, the SC prediction is used and the BPU issues a p3 redirect. The FTQ accepts 36 p3 redirects in FD09 (tb.n_redir_p3), and SC decided all of them. The monitor reads TAGE's own prediction and update signals, so SC changes none of the counts below.

docs.title: 4.2 Fetch block layout and update suppression in this run
docs.text:
Each fetch block has NUM_PRED_SLOTS prediction slots. A slot holds one conditional branch of the block, and TAGE predicts, updates and keeps its use_alt_on_na counter separately for each slot. With NUM_PRED_SLOTS = 1 every fetch block has one slot, slot 0, and the per-slot TAGE signals below are indexed [0].

With one slot an FTB entry holds one branch. When the back edge first resolves in the fetch block at top, the FTB splits the entry for top: it keeps B and ends that fetch block at the back edge's address, 0x8000_0016 (the split at update, planning/arch/ftb_decisions.md section 3, at cyc 32). From then on the block at top ends there, and the back edge is the first branch of the next fetch block, which starts at 0x8000_0016 and has its own FTB entry (allocated at cyc 43 and first predicted at cyc 46). After B is taken, fetch continues at 0x8000_0014; after a backend redirect for B not taken, at 0x8000_0012. The back edge is then the first branch of that block. Either way the back edge is in slot 0 of a fetch block of its own, at position 0, 1 or 2, and is predicted and trained with its own metadata. TAGE indexes its tables with the block's start address, so B's entries and the back edge's are separate. Both are in slot 0, so both train the one use_alt_on_na counter.

The loop's fetch blocks, read from the waveform, are shown below.

The back edge's first two resolutions, at cyc 21 and 32, came before the split took effect. Each was in a fetch block whose one slot held another branch, so its TAGE update was suppressed (rsv_plc_occ, rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_resolve.sv lines 46 to 57 and 443). TAGE takes 254 updates for the back edge, one for each of its other resolutions, and 256 for B.

docs.title: 4.3 Allocation
docs.text:
TAGE trains on its own prediction, whatever direction the front end finally used. When a conditional branch resolves, the FTQ's update conversion compares the TAGE direction carried with the branch with the resolved direction, and marks a TAGE misprediction when they differ. On a TAGE misprediction, when the provider is not T4, TAGE writes a new entry for the branch in a table with a longer history than the provider's. The table was chosen when the branch was predicted: the first longer-history table whose entry at the branch's index has an aged useful counter2 of 0. The new entry holds the branch's tag and starts at CTR 3'b100, the weakest taken value.

T0's entries start at 2'b10, weakly taken, so until T0 has learned B, TAGE predicts B taken. The first allocation is at cyc 20, for B on iteration 0: B was not taken and T0 had predicted it taken. The allocation comes from TAGE's misprediction alone; the backend's first misprediction, at cyc 21, is the back edge's.

Over the run TAGE mispredicted B on 58 of the 256 iterations: on 31 of the 33 iterations on which B was taken, and on 27 of the 223 on which it was not. Each of the 58 wrote an allocation. TAGE mispredicted the back edge once, when it fell through on iteration 255 (cyc 1355), and that wrote the 59th allocation. The allocations by table:

             T1   T2   T3   T4   total
B            11   12   28    7      58
back edge     1    0    0    0       1

The first taken B is on iteration 9. In the waveform, the backend resolves it at cyc 72: tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val is 1 and tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc is 0x8000_0014, B's target, because the front end fetched the fall-through. The allocation write is the next cycle, cyc 73, in the tage_update group:

  • tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.trx_type is 1 and tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.tage_upd_val_u0 is 1: the TAGE tables take an update this cycle. trx_type is an encoded field, 0 for a prediction cycle and 1 for an update cycle: it is the arbiter's grant (tage_arb.sv line 76), an input of tage_cntrl.sv (line 58), and the encoding is stated at rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_structs_pkg.sv line 314;
  • tb.dut.u_ftq.u_upd_conv.lp_upd_p0.[0].pc is 0x8000_000E, B's address (the TAGE update input has no address; the update conversion forms every predictor's update from one record, and the loop predictor's copy carries it);
  • tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.tage_upd_inp_u0.[0].cond_mispredict is 1 and .resolved_taken is 1; .tage_pred_meta.tage_prm_comp is 0, so T0 was the provider;
  • tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.u_alc_wr.[0] is 1 and tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.u_alc_comp.[0] is 1: the new entry is written into T1.

RTL: the TAGE misprediction is cond_mispredict, set in rtl/core/frontend/ftq/rtl/ftq_upd_conv.sv line 218. The candidate table is chosen at p1 in pred_logic, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/tage_cntrl.sv lines 574 to 585. The allocation is formed by alc_upd_comb in tage_cntrl.sv line 853, signal u_alc_wr. T0's starting value is TAGE_T0_SRAM_INIT_VALUE, rtl/core/frontend/bpu/rtl/bp_defines_pkg.sv line 418.

docs.title: 4.4 Training the use_alt_on_na counter
docs.text:
TAGE keeps a 4-bit counter, uaon, for each prediction slot. With one slot there is one counter, tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.uaon.[0]. It measures whether, when the provider's CTR is weak, the alternate has been more accurate than the provider. The rules are in planning/arch/tage_cntrl_uaon_update_rules.md: on an update whose prediction was weak, the counter increments when the provider was wrong and the alternate right, and decrements when the provider was right and the alternate wrong. It starts at 0.

uaon is updated only when both the provider and the alternate are tagged tables. When the alternate is T0, uaon is unchanged. The counter is therefore trained on predictions where two tagged tables matched. B and the back edge both update slot 0, so both could train the one counter; in this run only B's updates do. The back edge's predictions come from T0 until its single allocation on the last iteration, so none of its updates has a tagged provider.

The first prediction from a tagged table is at cyc 115. The history leading up to B is random, so the entries allocated for B are later matched under histories they were not trained on. Those entries are still weak, at CTR 3'b011 or 3'b100, and some predict taken for a branch taken only one time in eight. The table counts the updates that had a tagged provider, a tagged alternate and a weak prediction, by the provider and alternate tables and by what the update did to uaon. It increments when the provider was wrong and the alternate right, decrements when the provider was right and the alternate wrong, and is unchanged when the two predicted the same direction.

             T2 over T1   T3 over T2   increment   decrement   unchanged
B                    16            6          13           0           9
back edge             0            0           0           0           0
The update inputs are in the tage_update group: tage_upd_inp_u0.[0].tage_pred_meta.tage_prm_comp, .tage_alt_comp, .tage_pred_weak, .tage_prm_tkn and .tage_alt_tkn under tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.

In the waveform, uaon.[0] first reads 1 at cyc 225, the cycle of B's update with provider T2, predicting taken, and alternate T1, predicting not taken, weak; B was not taken, so the provider was wrong and the alternate right. No update decrements it. It reaches 8 at cyc 441 and its highest value, 13, at cyc 1031, below the counter's maximum of 15.

RTL: the update is uaon_upd_ff in tage_cntrl.sv line 380, and the condition that both tables are tagged is at lines 383 and 384 (u_prm_tagged and u_alt_tagged, defined at lines 670 and 671).

docs.title: 4.5 T0 provides through use_alt_on_na
docs.text:
When uaon reaches 8, its top bit is set. From then on, a prediction whose provider is a tagged table with a weak CTR uses the alternate instead of the provider. When no second tagged table matched, the alternate is T0, and the prediction comes from T0.

The counter that allows T0 to provide is trained only on predictions where the alternate was a tagged table, as section 4.4 describes. It then governs predictions where the alternate is T0. This follows the update rule in tage_cntrl_uaon_update_rules.md.

In the waveform, the first prediction from T0 through use_alt_on_na is at cyc 460, in slot 0, for the fetch block at top. In the tage_p2 group, tb.dut.u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.tage_pred_meta_p2.[0].tage_prm_comp is 1 (T1 matched B) and .tage_prm_ctr is 3'b100, weak; .tage_using_primary is 0 and .tage_alt_comp is 0, so the prediction is T0's, not taken. All 22 such predictions in the run have T1 as the provider, and all are TAGE answers for the block at top. The monitor counts TAGE answers whether or not the FTQ accepts the group, so a count can include an answer for a block on a wrong path.

RTL: the selection is in pred_logic in tage_cntrl.sv: the trigger, a tagged provider with a weak CTR, at lines 529 to 533, and the choice of the alternate when the trigger is set and uaon[s][3] is 1 at line 539. The result is registered into tage_pred_meta_p2 by meta_p2_ff at line 364.

  1. use_alt_on_na: use the alternate prediction table when the provider entry is newly allocated [1]. Pacino treats a provider entry with a weak CTR as newly allocated (section 4.5). ↩

  2. The useful counter USE is aged by the entry's epoch field EPC (see the entry format in section 4.1). Aging is disabled in every scenario: CSR 0x7C0 bit 2, tage_enable_aging, resets to 0 and no scenario sets it, so the epoch stays 0 and the aged useful counter equals USE. ↩

  3. FD09 runs with fast initialization, as every scenario but FD-1 does: a SystemVerilog initial block seeds each predictor table at time 0 and each predictor ties its ready to 1 (tage.sv line 333, the same in ittage.sv and sc.sv), so the table walks of FD-1 do not run. With the readies already 1, ftq_pred_val_p0 is 1 while tb.rstn is still low; the request is captured on the first cycle after reset. The common description describes fast initialization. ↩

  4. The Pacino TAGE design uses a consistent tag width for tables T1-T4, as in Seznec and Michaud's TAGE paper [1]. Other designs have used variable-width tag fields [2]. During performance analysis the benefits of variable-width tag fields will be evaluated. ↩

docs.title: fd10_pd_redirect: Predecode Redirect
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd10_pd_redirect (FD-10) runs a chain of 13 JALs to distinct prediction blocks, in a loop of 3 passes.

On the first pass, neither the uBTB nor the FTB holds any of the JALs, so each block is predicted to fall through. Predecode at F3 finds the JAL, the IFU writes the block back with a mispredict position, and the FTQ redirects the p0 request to the JAL's target. Once the predictors hold a block's JAL, that block needs no predecode redirect.

The FTQ takes 14 predecode redirects in the run. The result line in the log file reports that count.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

docs.title: 2. Run the scenario

Run simulation:

make -C examples/fe_demo view S=fd10_pd_redirect

Console output: 

-I: fd10_pd_redirect : PASS : cyc = 255

Log file output: 

-I: fd10_pd_redirect: PASS, predecode redirects 14, events checked 12 of 12,
    cyc 255

The testbench backend model supplies the count in the log line:

  • predecode redirects
    • n_pd_redir in rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_be_state.svh
    • cycles with u_ftq.w_pd_redir_val asserted and no backend redirect, while the expected instruction stream has not fully retired

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd10 in programs/fd10_pd_redirect.svh. The code consists of a short prologue, then a loop of 3 passes starting at top, and a short epilogue.

Each pass runs one jal at 0x8000_000A to T0, then 12 more through a chain of blocks. The last of them, in T11, goes to 0x8000_0108, where the back edge at 0x8000_010A returns to top. The back edge is taken on passes 0 and 1.

The program runs in machine mode with translation off, so the addresses are physical. The program starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv).

                                                           Position from
Address      Label  Instruction        Purpose             0x000  0x008
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1       ; prologue          0
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1   ; prologue          1
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1       ; prologue          3
0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1       ; filler            4      0
0x8000_000A         jal    x0, T0      ; first JAL         5      1

                                                           Position from T(k)
0x8000_0200  T0:    c.addi a0, 1       ; filler            0
0x8000_0202         addi   t0, t0, 1   ; filler            1
0x8000_0206         jal    x0, T1      ; chain JAL         3
                    ...                ; T(k) = 0x8000_0200 + k * 0x60
0x8000_0620  T11:   c.addi a0, 1       ; filler            0
0x8000_0622         addi   t0, t0, 1   ; filler            1
0x8000_0626         jal    x0, 0x108   ; last chain JAL    3

                                                           Position from 0x108
0x8000_0108         c.addi a0, 1       ; filler            0
0x8000_010A         bne    x6, x0, top ; back edge         1
0x8000_010E         c.addi a0, 1       ; epilogue          3
0x8000_0110         addi   t0, t0, 1   ; epilogue          4
0x8000_0114         c.addi a0, 1       ; epilogue          6
0x8000_0116  hold:  jal    x0, hold    ; termination       7

A position is the halfword offset of an instruction from the start of its prediction block. The 32-bit instructions take two positions. Each T(k) is 0x60 bytes from the last, so each JAL of the chain is in a different prediction block.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the branches.

The direction of the back edge is chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in it. The code is the same on every pass, and only the expected instruction stream changes.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text: Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

docs.title: 4.1 Finding the JALs at F3
docs.text:
A block with no taken slot is predicted to fall through, so ftq_ifu_taken_val is deasserted and the next request is the next sequential block. At F3, predecode marks each position's control transfer type. The first valid JAL in the block, before the predicted taken position if there is one, sets the mispredict position and is written back to the FTQ.1

The FTQ takes a writeback's mispredict position as a predecode redirect, with the corrected successor as the target.2 In the p0 arbiter, a predecode redirect ranks below a backend redirect and above the p3 and p2 redirects.3 Any redirect flushes the younger blocks in the IFU and rolls back the history.4

The first pass has the 13 redirects that the JALs give.

FTQ index   block   position   target   cyc
0           0x000   5          0x200    19
1           0x200   3          0x260    38
2           0x260   3          0x2C0    50
3           0x2C0   3          0x320    60
4           0x320   3          0x380    71
5           0x380   3          0x3E0    81
6           0x3E0   3          0x440    95
7           0x440   3          0x4A0    105
8           0x4A0   3          0x500    116
9           0x500   3          0x560    129
10          0x560   3          0x5C0    141
11          0x5C0   3          0x620    151
12          0x620   3          0x108    165

The first redirect is at cyc 19 (event 1), and the last of the pass at cyc 165 (event 2). In the meantime, the p0 request has run ahead sequentially. At cyc 19 the FTQ is presenting FTQ index 16 to the IFU, and the flush names index 1.

The block at 0x8000_0108 holds the back edge at position 1 and the hold JAL at position 7. The back edge is not known yet, so predecode finds the JAL. Its redirect to 0x8000_0116 is at cyc 175 (event 3), the same cycle as the backend's redirect for the back edge to top (event 4). The backend redirect wins, so the monitor does not count this one.

The backend redirect starts the p0 request at top, a block start that has not been seen before, because the first pass started its block at 0x8000_0000. An FTB entry belongs to one block start, so the jal at 0x8000_000A is unknown in this block. Predecode finds it at position 1, and the 14th counted redirect is at cyc 186 (event 5). It is the last in the run.

From there on, the JALs are predicted. The uBTB supplies the block at 0x8000_0200 at p1 at cyc 187 (event 6), and the FTB confirms it at p2 at cyc 188 (event 7). The rest of the chain follows in order, to the block at 0x8000_0620 at cyc 203 (event 8). In these blocks the p2 slot agrees with the p1 slot, so there is no p2 redirect. Pass 2 starts with the block at top, predicted at p1 for the first time at cyc 209 (event 9).

The back edge is predicted taken in passes 1 and 2. In pass 2 it falls through, and the backend redirects to 0x8000_010E at cyc 245 (event 10).

docs.title: 4.2 The redirect in the waveform
docs.text:
The waveform group ifu_f3 shows the writeback and the redirect, and ftq_ifu shows the flush and the requests that follow.

At cyc 19 (event 1), ifu_ftq_pdwb_val is asserted with ifu_ftq_pdwb_idx 0. ifu_ftq_mis_val is asserted with ifu_ftq_mis_pos 5, and ifu_ftq_target is 0x8000_0200. u_ftq.w_pd_redir_val is asserted in the same cycle, with u_ftq.w_pd_redir_pc 0x8000_0200. ftq_pred_pc_p0 is 0x8000_0200, and ftq_ifu_flush_val is asserted with ftq_ifu_flush_idx 1. At cyc 22, ftq_ifu_req_val is asserted with ftq_ifu_idx 1 and ftq_ifu_start_pc 0x8000_0200.

At cyc 175 (events 3 and 4), w_pd_redir_val and tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val are both asserted. w_pd_redir_pc is 0x8000_0116 and tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc is 0x8000_0008, and ftq_pred_pc_p0 follows the backend's redirect.

At cyc 187 (event 6), u_bpu.r_pc_p1 is 0x8000_0200 and u_bpu.r_ubtb_blk_p1.hit is asserted. bpu_pred_slot_p1.[0] is a DIRECT_UNC with target 0x8000_0260 and pred_src PRED_UBTB.

At cyc 188 (event 7), u_bpu.r_pc_p2 is 0x8000_0200 and bpu_slot_p2.[0] holds the JAL at pos 3 with pred_src PRED_FTB. ftq_ifu_taken_val is asserted and ftq_ifu_next_pc is 0x8000_0260. No writeback for this block carries ifu_ftq_mis_val.

During the drain after cyc 255, w_pd_redir_val asserts about every 9 cycles for the hold JAL. The monitor does not count these.

docs.text: # cyc Event Other 0 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests 0x8000_0000 the same cycle fast init 1 19 first predecode redirect: the jal at top + 2, found at F3, to T(0), 0x8000_0200 pass 0 2 165 the 13th predecode redirect: the jal of T(11), to 0x8000_0108 pass 0 3 175 a predecode redirect to 0x8000_0116, the halt's jal fetched past the cold back edge; the backend's redirect takes the next request, so the monitor does not count it not counted 4 175 the back edge mispredicted, cold; redirect to 0x8000_0008 backend 5 186 last predecode redirect: the jal at top + 2 again, to 0x8000_0200, in the block that starts at top pass 1, the 14th counted 6 187 first chain JAL predicted at p1: the block at 0x8000_0200, from the uBTB pred_src PRED_UBTB 7 188 first chain JAL predicted at p2: the block at 0x8000_0200, from the FTB pred_src PRED_FTB 8 203 last chain JAL of pass 1 predicted at p1: the block at 0x8000_0620 16 cycles from event 6 9 209 top's jal first predicted at p1: the block at 0x8000_0008 pass 2 10 245 back edge falls through, a misprediction; redirect to 0x8000_010E pass 2, backend 11 255 the run ends a 100 cycle drain follows, to 355

docs.title: fd11_be_mispredict: Backend Mispredict
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd11_be_mispredict (FD-11) runs a conditional with a pseudo-random outcome, then a call and its return, in a loop of 32 passes.

The conditional's outcome has no pattern for the predictors to learn, so the backend often resolves it against the prediction and redirects. In the redirect cycle, the FTQ squashes the younger entries and flushes the IFU, the history rolls back and takes the corrected outcome, and the RAS restores its pointers from the entry's snapshot. Fetch then restarts at the corrected PC.

The backend raises 21 mispredict redirects in the run, and the first fetch after each one starts at the redirect PC. The result line in the log file reports those counts.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

docs.title: 1.1 Files
docs.text:

docs.title: 2. Run the scenario
docs.text:
Run simulation:

View the waveform (runs simulation first if FST is not up to date): 

make -C examples/fe_demo view S=fd11_be_mispredict

Console output: 

-I: fd11_be_mispredict : PASS : cyc = 480

Log file output: 

-I: fd11_be_mispredict: PASS, backend mispredict redirects 21,
    fetches at the redirect address 21, history rollbacks 82, RAS restores 82,
    events checked 18 of 18, cyc 480

The testbench monitor (examples/fe_demo/tb/fe_demo_mon.svh) supplies the counts in the log line:

  • backend mispredict redirects
    • n_be_misp
    • cycles with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val asserted and tb.bkend_ftq_redir_cause RC_MISPREDICT
  • fetches at the redirect address
    • n_be_fix
    • redirects whose first following fetch, with ftq_ifu_req_val and ftq_ifu_req_rdy asserted and no flush, has ftq_ifu_start_pc equal to the redirect PC
  • history rollbacks
    • n_rollback
    • cycles with ftq_rollback_val asserted, for a redirect from any source
  • RAS restores
    • n_ras_rest
    • cycles with ras_restore_val asserted, the same net as ftq_rollback_val

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd11 in programs/fd11_be_mispredict.svh. The code consists of a short prologue, then a loop of 32 passes starting at top, and a short epilogue.

Each pass runs the conditional A, then a call to fn from 0x8000_0010, and the return to 0x8000_0014. The back edge at 0x8000_0016 returns to top. The back edge is taken on passes 0 to 30.

The program runs in machine mode with translation off, so the addresses are physical. The program starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv).

                                                         Position from
Address      Label  Instruction           Purpose        0x000 0x008 0x00E 0x010
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1          ; prologue     0
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1      ; prologue     1
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1          ; prologue     3
0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1          ; filler       4     0
0x8000_000A  A:     bne    x6, x0, 0x010  ; conditional  5     1
0x8000_000E         c.addi a0, 1          ; skipped by A 7     3     0
0x8000_0010         jal    x1, fn         ; call         8     4     1     0

                                                         Position from 0x014
0x8000_0014         c.addi a0, 1          ; return point 0
0x8000_0016  E:     bne    x6, x0, top    ; back edge    1
0x8000_001A         c.addi a0, 1          ; epilogue     3
0x8000_001C         addi   t0, t0, 1      ; epilogue     4
0x8000_0020         c.addi a0, 1          ; epilogue     6
0x8000_0022  hold:  jal    x0, hold       ; termination  7

                                                         Position from 0x400
0x8000_0400  fn:    c.addi a0, 1          ; filler       0
0x8000_0402         addi   t0, t0, 1      ; filler       1
0x8000_0406         ret                   ; return       3

A position is the halfword offset of an instruction from the start of its prediction block. The 32-bit instructions take two positions. The four position columns at the top are the block starts that hold these instructions in the run.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the branches.

The direction of A is one bit per pass from the program writer's 16-bit Galois LFSR, with taps 0xB400 and seed 0xACE1 (lfsr_bit in rtl/core/frontend/fe_top/tb/models/fe_tb_writer.svh). From pass 0 to pass 31 the bits are:

1000 0111 0010 0011 0100 0110 1101 1100

A bit of 1 is taken, which skips the c.addi at 0x8000_000E. A is taken on 15 passes and not taken on 17. The direction is resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in it. The code is the same on every pass, and only the expected instruction stream changes.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text: Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform. A signal the testbench drives, such as tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val, changes one time unit after the clock edge, so a backend redirect reads at the marker of the next cycle.

docs.title: 4.1 The backend redirect
docs.text:
The backend model retires the bundle against the expected instruction stream. When the instruction after a control transfer is not the expected one, it raises tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val with cause RC_MISPREDICT, the FTQ index and position of the transfer, the resolved direction and the correct PC.1

In the FTQ's p0 arbiter a backend redirect outranks every other redirect, without comparison.2 In the redirect cycle:

  • ftq_pred_pc_p0 is the redirect PC, and ftq_pred_idx_p0 is the entry after the named one. The younger entries are squashed.
  • ftq_ifu_flush_val is asserted, naming that same entry.3
  • ftq_rollback_val is asserted, with ftq_rollback_corr.4
  • ras_restore_val is asserted, with the named entry's RAS snapshot.5

The run has 21 backend redirects, and all have cause RC_MISPREDICT and tb.bkend_ftq_redir_self deasserted.

All 21 first fetches start at the redirect PC. The p0 request is held in every redirect cycle by the FTB update scheduler, so ftq_pred_val_p0 is deasserted while ftq_pred_pc_p0 shows the redirect PC.6 The request becomes valid 1 or 2 cycles after cyc, and the first fetch is 3 to 5 cycles after cyc.

docs.title: 4.2 The branches the backend redirects
docs.text:
A's first redirect is at cyc 20 (event 2), at position 5 of the block at 0x8000_0000, before any predictor holds it. Fetch restarts at 0x8000_0010 at cyc 23 (event 3). The return and the back edge are first redirected at cyc 49 (event 5) and cyc 60 (event 7), and fetch restarts at 0x8000_0014 at cyc 53 (event 6).

A is redirected in 18 of the 32 passes, 8 times to 0x8000_0010 and 10 times to 0x8000_000E. No backend redirect names A in passes 1, 3, 4, 7, 14, 15, 16, 17, 22, 25, 26, 28, 30 and 31. The first redirect of A not taken is at cyc 86 in pass 2 (event 12), and fetch restarts at 0x8000_000E at cyc 89 (event 13).

The FTB update at cyc 82 (event 10) records the call at position 4 of the block at top. A already holds the entry's one slot, so the FTB splits the entry at the call, with upd_cut_pos 4, and the block at top now ends at 0x8000_0010. From then on, both predicted directions of A continue at the block at 0x8000_0010. A predicted taken ends the fetch at A, and A predicted not taken also fetches the c.addi at 0x8000_000E. The block at 0x8000_000E is used only after a backend redirect to it.

The back edge is not redirected again until it falls through in pass 31, at cyc 471 (event 15), and fetch restarts at 0x8000_001A at cyc 474 (event 16). The return is not redirected again at all.

docs.title: 4.3 The other redirects
docs.text:
The 82 rollbacks in the log line are the redirects the FTQ takes from all sources, up to cyc 480.

Source      Count   Target    Branch
backend     21                section 4.1
predecode   3       0x400     the call
p3          2       0x010     A
p2          56      0x014     the return

The predecode redirects are for the call, once in each block start that holds it. These are position 0 of the block at 0x8000_0010 at cyc 29 (event 4), position 4 of the block at 0x8000_0008 at cyc 69, and position 1 of the block at 0x8000_000E at cyc 95. A predecode redirect is also asserted at cyc 19 and cyc 59, so the marker of cyc 19 shows the rollback of event 1 with the predecode redirect's values. The backend redirect rises one time unit later in both cycles and wins.

The p3 redirects are at cyc 76 (event 9) and cyc 83, and both take A to 0x8000_0010. The p2 redirects start at cyc 72 (event 8). A uBTB return slot is taken at p1 only when the stack read at p1 is valid.7 On 57 of the 61 p1 slots accepted for the block at 0x8000_0400 it is not valid, so the slot is not taken and p2 redirects to 0x8000_0014.

docs.title: 4.4 The history rollback
docs.text:
bp_history moves the pointer back to the first bit of the entry the rollback names, writes the corrected outcome bits, advances past them, and records the corrected bundle in that entry's checkpoint.8 Each backend redirect in this run writes one bit, the resolved direction of the branch.

In the first three redirects the pointer moves forward by the one corrected bit, because no younger entry has advanced it. The rollback at cyc 86 is the first to move it back. The speculative stream has advanced bpu_ghist_ptr to 10, and rolling back to FTQ index 7 leaves it at 6 at cyc 86.

The backend model checks the corrected bit in the cycle after a redirect of a conditional: the history bit before the pointer must equal the resolved direction.9 Its counters tb.n_hist_ok and tb.n_hist_bad end at 20 and 0, for 18 redirects of A and 2 of the back edge. The return's redirect is not checked.

docs.title: 4.5 The RAS restore
docs.text:
The restore is pointer-only. TOSR, TOSW and BOS load from the entry's snapshot, and the stack data is not cleared.10

ras_restore_val is asserted for all 82 redirects, and bp_cluster drops the restore when the redirect is the block's own p2 or p3 redirect.11 That leaves 24 restores that reach the RAS, from the 21 backend redirects and the 3 predecode redirects.

The first restore to move a pointer is at cyc 86 (event 11), where TOSW goes from 2 to 0. The first to move BOS is at cyc 125 (event 14), where TOSR, TOSW and BOS go from 4/5/2 to 1/3/1. In all 17 redirects of A after cyc 19, TOSW moves back. The pointers wrap at 16 entries, as the rows from cyc 298 show. After pass 0, the backend redirects no return.

docs.title: 4.6 The redirect in the waveform
docs.text:
The redirect at cyc 86 shows each part. The waveform group backend shows the redirect, bp_cluster_p0 the p0 request, ftq_ifu the flush and the restart, and bp_history_ras the rollback and the restore.

At cyc 85, bpu_ghist_ptr is 10 and u_bpu.u_ras.tosw is 2.

At cyc 86 (events 11 and 12), tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val is asserted with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_idx 7, tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pos 1, tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc 0x8000_000E and tb.bkend_ftq_redir_taken 0. ftq_pred_pc_p0 is 0x8000_000E and ftq_pred_idx_p0 is 8, while u_ftq.u_npc.w_hold holds the request. ftq_ifu_flush_val is asserted with ftq_ifu_flush_idx 8. ftq_rollback_val and ftq_rollback_corr are asserted with ftq_rollback_idx 7. bpu_ghist_ptr is 6 and u_bpu.u_ras.tosw is 0, because these registers load at the clock edge at this marker. One time unit later the redirect falls, and ftq_pred_val_p0 is asserted with ftq_pred_pc_p0 0x8000_000E.

At cyc 89 (event 13), ftq_ifu_req_val and ftq_ifu_req_rdy are asserted with ftq_ifu_idx 8 and ftq_ifu_start_pc 0x8000_000E.

The figure below shows these cycles.

docs.title: fd12_training: Predictor Training
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd12_training (FD-12) shows resolved branches initiating update requests routed to the respective predictor based on branch type. It also illustrates the operation of the single ported FTB.

The scenario runs an outer loop of 14 iterations, containing an inner loop of 6 iterations. The outer loop includes:

1. an always-taken conditional
2. an indirect jump
3. an indirect call and its return.

The inner loop includes a backward branch executing the stated 6 iterations.

This code then results in all predictors receiving illustrative updates.

Each executed branch is resolved by the backend, converted by ftq_upd_conv into per-predictor updates, and presented to the cluster.

An FTB update is a read-modify-write and occupies the single FTB read port for one cycle. Prediction lookups use the same port at p1. To avoid the conflict, the FTQ stalls its prediction request in the cycle before each FTB update.

The result line in the log file reports the update count for each predictor and the number of FTQ prediction request stall cycles.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd12 in programs/fd12_training.svh. The code consists of an arbitrary prologue, then the outer loop of 14 passes starting at otop, and a short epilogue. The inner loop of 6 passes starts at itop.

Each outer pass runs the inner loop, then the always-taken beq (B:), the indirect jump (J:), the indirect call (K:) to fn and its return, then the outer loop branch (O:) returning to otop.

The inner loop branch (I:) and the outer loop branch (O:) are taken on every execution except the last iterations.

The beq (B:) operand selection, x0 and x0, results in the branch always being taken. This is configured to illustrate conditional branch training behavior.

The program runs in machine mode with translation off, so the addresses are physical. The program starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv).

Address      Label  Instruction             Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0008         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue

0x8000_000A  otop:  c.addi a0, 1            ; outer body
0x8000_000C         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; outer body

0x8000_0010  itop:  c.addi a0, 1            ; inner body
0x8000_0012         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; inner body
0x8000_0016         c.addi a0, 1            ; inner body
0x8000_0018  I:     bne    x6, x0, itop     ; inner loop branch
0x8000_001C  B:     beq    x0, x0, 0x028    ; always taken

0x8000_0028         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8000_002A         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8000_002E  J:     jalr   x0, 0(x7)        ; indirect jump, to 0x06E

0x8000_006E         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8000_0070         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8000_0074  K:     jalr   x1, 0(x28)       ; indirect call, to fn
0x8000_0078         c.addi a0, 1            ; after the return
0x8000_007A  O:     bne    x6, x0, otop     ; outer loop branch

0x8000_007E         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_0080         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8000_0084         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_0086  hold:  jal    x0, hold         ; termination

0x8000_0800  fn:    c.addi a0, 1            ; function body
0x8000_0802         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; function body
0x8000_0806         ret                     ; return to 0x8000_0078

The indirect jump (J:) is an INDIRECT_NONRET because neither register is a link register, and the indirect call (K:) is an INDIRECT_CALL because rd is x1. The ret in fn is a RETURN.

With one prediction slot, an FTB entry holds one branch, so the path is predicted as several blocks. The accepted p2 slot groups, by block:

Block start Reached by Branch Position Block end Groups 0x8000_000A the outer loop branch taken inner loop branch (I:) 7 0x8000_002A 13 0x8000_0010 itop inner loop branch (I:) 4 0x8000_0030 before the split 26 0x8000_0010 itop inner loop branch (I:) 4 0x8000_001C after the split 65 0x8000_001C the inner loop branch not taken always-taken beq (B:) 0 0x8000_003C 14 0x8000_0028 the beq taken indirect jump (J:) 3 0x8000_0032 13 0x8000_006E the indirect jump indirect call (K:) 3 0x8000_0078 13 0x8000_0800 the indirect call ret 4 0x8000_080C 13 0x8000_0078 the return outer loop branch (O:) 1 0x8000_0098 13

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the branches.

The directions and targets are chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in them. x7 and x28 are never read.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows branch resolutions from the backend model to the predictor updates.

Section 4.1 describes update generation and qualification by branch type. Section 4.2 shows the FTB update/FTQ stall conditions. Section 4.3 describes the one resolution in the run that does not train the loop predictor, TAGE and SC, and the FTB entry split that accompanies it.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform. A signal the testbench drives, such as tb.bkend_ftq_rsv_val, changes one time unit after the clock edge, as does logic combinational from it, so the waveform first shows the new value at the marker of the next cycle.

The waveform group bp_cluster_update contains the update valids after the bp_cluster qualification, ftb_update the FTB update, and bp_cluster_p0 the p0 request and its stall.

docs.title: 4.1 Predictor update generation and branch type qualification
docs.text:
Module ftq_upd_conv generates the update inputs for the predictors, with the exceptions of FTB and RAS. A slot's update valids are asserted only when every predictor that the slot trains can accept the update.1

bp_cluster decodes the branch type of each update from its uBTB update input and qualifies the per-predictor valids as follows:2

Predictor        Trained on
uBTB             all branch types except NO_BRANCH
loop predictor   COND
TAGE, SC         COND; each also qualified by its queue ready, SC by sc_enable
ITTAGE           INDIRECT_NONRET, INDIRECT_CALL
FTB              conditional or jump, on the dedicated ftb_upd_* channel
RAS commit       DIRECT_CALL, INDIRECT_CALL, RETURN, RETURN_CALL

The first resolution is that of the inner loop branch (I:), at position 12 of the block at 0x8000_0000, at cyc 21 (event 1). This COND resolution produces the first uBTB, FTB, loop predictor, TAGE and SC updates. The indirect jump (J:) produces the first ITTAGE update at cyc 66 (event 3). The indirect call (K:) produces the first RAS commit at cyc 78 (event 4), one cycle after its resolution at cyc 77. The first RETURN commit follows at cyc 98 (event 5).

At cyc 21 (event 1), tb.bkend_ftq_rsv_val is asserted. u_bpu.w_ubtb_upd_u0.[0].valid is asserted with .pc 0x8000_0000 and .pos 12. u_ftq.u_upd_conv.lp_upd_p0.[0].pc is 0x8000_0018, the address of the inner loop branch (I:). u_bpu.w_lp_upd_val_p0, u_bpu.w_tage_upd_val_u0 and u_bpu.w_sc_upd_val_u0 are asserted. ftb_upd_valid_u0 is asserted with ftb_upd_pc_u0 0x8000_0000, ftb_upd_pos_u0 12, ftb_upd_is_br_u0 1 and ftb_upd_hit_u0 0.

At cyc 66 (event 3), u_bpu.w_ittage_upd_val_u0 is asserted and lp_upd_p0.[0].pc is 0x8000_002E, the address of the indirect jump (J:). ftb_upd_is_jmp_u0 is 1.

At cyc 78 (event 4), u_bpu.w_ras_commit_val is asserted with ras_commit_br_type INDIRECT_CALL and ras_commit_ret_addr 0x8000_0078.

At cyc 98 (event 5), u_bpu.w_ras_commit_val is asserted with ras_commit_br_type RETURN.

The run contains 15 backend redirects:

docs.title: 4.2 p0 request stall for FTB updates
docs.text:
The FTB has a single read port. When ftq_ftb_sched will issue an FTB update in the next cycle, a p0 request in the current cycle would reach its FTB read at p1 in that cycle, so ftq_npc stalls the request.3 Each FTB update stalls the p0 request for one cycle, 154 cycles in the run. The first stall is for the FTB update at cyc 21 (event 1).

At cyc 21 (event 1), u_ftq.u_npc.h3_ftb_upd and u_ftq.u_npc.w_hold are asserted, and ftq_pred_val_p0 is deasserted with ftq_pred_pc_p0 0x8000_0010. These signals transition one time unit after the marker of cyc 20. One time unit after the marker of cyc 21, the stall ends and ftq_pred_val_p0 asserts with the same PC. ftb_upd_valid_u0 remains asserted until the marker of cyc 22. The stall therefore occupies the clock cycle preceding the FTB update.

FTB updates can occur in consecutive cycles, each with its own stall. The first such sequence is four updates of the inner loop branch (I:), from cyc 42 (event 2) to cyc 45. u_ftq.u_npc.h3_ftb_upd remains asserted and ftq_pred_val_p0 remains deasserted from one time unit after the marker of cyc 41 until one time unit after the marker of cyc 45, so no prediction request is presented in those four cycles.

The figure below shows these cycles.

docs.title: 4.3 Suppressed training for a resolution placed in an occupied slot
docs.text:
In pass 2, the block at 0x8000_0010 contains both the inner loop branch (I:) at position 4 and the always-taken beq (B:) at position 6, and the FTB entry's single slot holds the inner loop branch. The backend redirects to 0x8000_0028 at cyc 166 (event 6), and the beq resolves at cyc 168 (event 7). The FTQ places the resolution in the occupied slot, whose prediction metadata describes the inner loop branch, and suppresses the loop predictor, TAGE and SC updates.4 The uBTB and FTB updates are still generated, and the FTB update splits the entry so that the block thereafter ends at 0x8000_001C. The FTQ accepts the first p2 group with the new block end at cyc 176 (event 8). This is the only such placement in the run, so the loop predictor, TAGE and SC counts are 111, not 112.

The figure below shows the block before and after the split.

At cyc 166 (event 6), tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val is asserted with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc 0x8000_0028, tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pos 6 and tb.bkend_ftq_redir_taken 1.

At cyc 168 (event 7), u_ftq.u_resolve.rsv_plc_occ is asserted. u_bpu.w_ubtb_upd_u0.[0].valid is asserted with .pc 0x8000_0010 and .pos 6, and lp_upd_p0.[0].pc is 0x8000_001C. w_lp_upd_val_p0, w_tage_upd_val_u0 and w_sc_upd_val_u0 are deasserted. ftb_upd_valid_u0 is asserted with ftb_upd_pos_u0 6, ftb_upd_hit_u0 1, u_bpu.u_ftb.u_ftb_cntrl.upd_split 1 and u_bpu.u_ftb.u_ftb_cntrl.upd_cut_pos 6.

At cyc 176 (event 8), u_ftq.w_ok_slot_p2 is asserted with u_bpu.r_pc_p2 0x8000_0010 and bpu_blk_pft_p2 0x8000_001C. bpu_slot_p2.[0].pos is 4.

docs.title: FD-13 L1I Hit, Miss and MSHR Merge
fd13_l1i: L1I Hit, Miss and MSHR Merge
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd13_l1i (FD-13) shows the three L1I outcomes for a fetch request:

  1. a 2-cycle hit returning a full line
  2. a miss with an MSHR fill
  3. a second request merged onto a miss already in flight.

The program runs a loop of 8 iterations within one 64-byte cache line, which produces the hits. After the initial line fill, the loop's fetch requests hit in the L1I.

The program then calls a function whose entry is in the upper half of a line X, three times. These calls train the predictors.

A FENCE.I then invalidates all L1I lines, while leaving the predictor state intact. The program makes a fourth call to the function.

The prediction block at the call target requires lines X and X+1, so the IFU requests both. The predicted successor block then requests line X while its miss is outstanding, and the MSHR merges this request onto the register already fetching the line.

The result line in the log file reports the hits, misses and merges.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

docs.text:
