docs.title: 2. Run the scenario
docs.text:
Run simulation: 

make -C examples/fe_demo fd13_l1i

View the waveform (runs simulation first if FST is not up to date): 

make -C examples/fe_demo view S=fd13_l1i

Console output: 

-I: fd13_l1i : PASS : cyc = 214

Log file output: 

-I: fd13_l1i: PASS, L1I hits 48, L1I misses 29, merges 1,
    events checked 11 of 11, cyc 214

The testbench monitor, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh, supplies the counts in the log line, while the expected instruction stream has not fully retired. Hits and misses are bank lookups: a block that needs two lines counts two lookups, a merged request counts none, and wrong-path requests are counted.

Item Counter Counted L1I hits n_l1i_hit u_l1i.b_rsp_valid[b], summed over the banks L1I misses n_l1i_miss u_l1i.b_mis_valid[b], summed over the banks merges n_l1i_merge u_l1i.u_mshr.accept and u_l1i.u_mshr.mrg_hit

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd13 in programs/fd13_l1i.svh. The code consists of a short prologue, a loop of 8 passes starting at top, four calls to X30, and a short epilogue. X is the line at 0x8000_0800 and X+1 the line at 0x8000_0840.

Each call goes to X30, in the upper half of line X. The jump at X30 + 2 (J:) goes back to the start of line X, and the return (R:) goes back to the instruction after the call. A FENCE.I and 24 filler instructions precede the fourth call.

The program runs in machine mode with translation off, so the addresses are physical. The program starts at the reset vector, RESET_VECTOR = 0x8000_0000 (bp_defines_pkg.sv).

Address      Label  Instruction             Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; prologue

0x8000_0006  top:   c.addi a0, 1            ; loop body
0x8000_0008         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; loop body
0x8000_000C         c.addi a0, 1            ; loop body
0x8000_000E         c.addi a0, 1            ; loop body
0x8000_0010         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; loop body
0x8000_0014         c.addi a0, 1            ; loop body
0x8000_0016  L:     bne    x6, x0, top      ; loop branch, 8 passes

0x8000_001A  C1:    jal    x1, X30          ; first call
0x8000_001E         c.addi a0, 1            ; after the return
0x8000_0020  C2:    jal    x1, X30          ; second call
0x8000_0024         c.addi a0, 1            ; after the return
0x8000_0026  C3:    jal    x1, X30          ; third call
0x8000_002A         c.addi a0, 1            ; after the return

0x8000_002C         fence.i                 ; every L1I line invalid
0x8000_0030         c.addi, addi, ...       ; 24 fillers, to 0x8000_006F
0x8000_0070  C4:    jal    x1, X30          ; fourth call
0x8000_0074         c.addi a0, 1            ; after the return

0x8000_0076         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_0078         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8000_007C         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_007E  hold:  jal    x0, hold         ; termination

0x8000_0800  X:     c.addi a0, 1            ; start of line X
0x8000_0802         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8000_0806  R:     ret                     ; return

0x8000_0830  X30:   c.addi a0, 1            ; upper half of line X
0x8000_0832  J:     jal    x0, X            ; back to the start of line X

The loop, from 0x8000_0006 to 0x8000_001A, stays within the line at 0x8000_0000. A block that starts in the upper half of a line requires that line and the next, so the block at X30 requests lines X and X+1.

The FENCE.I invalidates every L1I line, and the predictors keep what the first three calls trained. The front end fetches ahead of the backend, so the fetch continues past the FENCE.I before the restart. The 24 fillers, one 64-byte line, keep that fetch from requesting line X before the fourth call.

With one prediction slot, an FTB entry holds one branch. The accepted p2 slot groups, by block:

Block start Reached by Branch Position Block end Groups 0x8000_0006 top L: 8 0x8000_0026 10 0x8000_0830 a call J: 1 0x8000_0836 4 0x8000_0800 J: R: 3 0x8000_080A 4

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the branches.

The directions and targets are chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in them.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows requests from the IFU through the L1I. Section 4.1 describes a hit, section 4.2 a miss and its fill, and section 4.3 the merge.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform. A signal the testbench drives, such as tb.l1i_mem_d_valid, changes one time unit after the clock edge, so the waveform first shows the new value at the marker of the next cycle.

The waveform group ifu_l1i contains the requests and responses, and l1i the bank results, the MSHR registers and the memory port.

docs.title: 4.1 L1I hit
docs.text:
The L1I read latency is 2 cycles. A hit produces the response from the bank's compare stage, carrying the full 64-byte line on l1i_ifu_rsp_data.1 The first hit after the cold fills complete is in the loop, at cyc 35 (event 4).

At cyc 35 (event 4), ifu_l1i_req_val and ifu_l1i_req_rdy are asserted with ifu_l1i_req_id 0 and ifu_l1i_req_paddr 0x8000_0000. At cyc 36, u_l1i.b_rsp_valid.[0] is asserted. At cyc 37, l1i_ifu_rsp_val is asserted with l1i_ifu_rsp_id 0.

The first hit in the run is earlier, at cyc 26 (event 3), while cold fills are still in progress.

docs.title: 4.2 L1I miss and fill
docs.text:
A miss is reported in the same compare stage, for the MSHR register allocated when the request was accepted, and the line is fetched through the memory port.2 The first miss is the line at 0x8000_0000.

At cyc 4, the request is accepted with ifu_l1i_req_id 0. At cyc 5 (event 1), u_l1i.b_mis_valid.[0] and u_l1i.u_mshr.e_val.[0] are asserted. At cyc 6 (event 2), tb.l1i_mem_a_valid is asserted with tb.l1i_mem_a_address 0x8000_0000 and tb.l1i_mem_a_source 0. The memory response beats are at cyc 14 and 15, with tb.l1i_mem_d_source 0. At cyc 15, u_l1i.u_mshr.b_fil_valid.[0] writes the line into the array. At cyc 16, u_l1i.u_mshr.e_got.[0] and l1i_ifu_rsp_val are asserted with l1i_ifu_rsp_id 0.

docs.title: 4.3 MSHR merge
docs.text:
After the FENCE.I, the block at X30 requests lines X and X+1, then the predicted block at X requests line X again. The IFU reuses a line only when the block's first line equals the line of the previous request.3 The previous request is X+1, so the block at X issues its own request. A block on the same line as the previous request never merges, because the IFU reuses that line.

The MSHR finds a valid register for line X whose data has not arrived, and sets mrg_hit. A merged request does not look up the arrays.4 Line X therefore has one memory request, and its fill answers both requests.

At cyc 176 (event 7), the fourth call is found at F3: u_ftq.w_pd_redir_val is asserted with u_ftq.w_pd_redir_pc 0x8000_0830.

At cyc 181, ifu_l1i_req_id 0 requests 0x8000_0800. At cyc 182, id 4 requests 0x8000_0840. At cyc 183 (event 8), id 1 requests 0x8000_0800, with u_l1i.u_mshr.accept and u_l1i.u_mshr.mrg_hit asserted. u_l1i.u_mshr.e_val.[0] is asserted and u_l1i.u_mshr.e_got.[0] is deasserted. tb.l1i_mem_a_valid is asserted with address 0x8000_0800 and source 0, the only memory request for line X after the FENCE.I.

The memory response beats with source 0 are at cyc 191 and 192. At cyc 192, u_l1i.u_mshr.b_fil_valid.[0] writes the line. At cyc 193, l1i_ifu_rsp_val is asserted with l1i_ifu_rsp_id 0, and at cyc 194 (event 9) with l1i_ifu_rsp_id 1, the merged request. Line X+1 is answered at cyc 198, with l1i_ifu_rsp_id 4.

The figure below shows these cycles.

mrg_hit is the MSHR's match of the presented request, so it is also asserted in cycles with no request taken. The merge count therefore also requires u_l1i.u_mshr.accept.

docs.title: fd14_translation: Sv39 Walk, Sv39x4 Nested Walk and Svadu CAS
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd14_translation (FD-14) demonstrates instruction address translation:

  1. an ITLB miss and an Sv39 page table walk
  2. a Svadu A-bit update by compare-and-swap
  3. a nested Sv39x4 walk, which translates through the VS-stage and the G-stage

The program first executes in supervisor mode under single-stage Sv39 translation1, with hardware update of the PTE accessed (A) bit enabled. The leaf PTE of its code page has the A bit clear, so the page table walk sets the bit by compare-and-swap.

An ecall then transfers execution to a guest under two-stage translation, and fetches in the guest walk both stages. Section 4 defines the RISC-V terms.

The result line in the log file reports the walks by kind, the G-stage PTE evaluations and the compare-and-swaps.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd14 in programs/fd14_translation.svh. The code consists of a short prologue at the reset vector, a body on page C ending in an ecall, and a body on page V.

The program executes in S-mode under satp Sv39 with ASID 1 and root 0x8F00_0000, with menvcfg.ADUE set. Page V is reached in VS-mode, under vsatp Sv39 with ASID 1 and hgatp Sv39x4 with VMID 3 and root 0x8E00_0000.

The change of privilege is applied by the testbench. When the ecall retires, the testbench sets V=1, privilege S, vsatp and hgatp, in place of the trap to M-mode and the return to VS-mode that software would execute.2 The backend's trap redirect then fetches V.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the control transfers.

The run has no accepted p2 slot groups, because no block repeats and the FTB therefore never hits.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows the translation of each code page. Section 4.1 describes an ITLB miss and a single-stage walk, section 4.2 the Svadu A-bit update, and section 4.3 the nested walk.

The RISC-V terms used below are as follows. Sv39 is the 3-level page table format with 39-bit virtual addresses, rooted at the CSR satp. Under the hypervisor extension, V=1 selects guest execution: VS-mode is the guest's supervisor mode, the VS-stage is the guest's translation, under the CSR vsatp, and the G-stage is the hypervisor's second-level translation, under the CSR hgatp. Sv39x4 is the G-stage format for Sv39 guests, with 41-bit guest physical addresses and a 16 KiB root table. Svadu is the extension under which hardware updates a PTE's accessed (A) and dirty (D) bits. menvcfg.ADUE enables it for single-stage and G-stage translation. Without it, a clear A bit raises a page fault for software to handle (Svade).

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform. A signal the testbench drives, such as tb.mem_ptw_rsp_val, changes one time unit after the clock edge, so the waveform first shows the new value at the marker of the next cycle.

The waveform group itlb contains the IFU lookups, walker the ITLB requests, tb.u_ptw.r_st and the responses, and walker_mem the walker's memory port.

docs.title: 4.1 ITLB miss and single-stage walk
docs.text:
The first fetch misses the ITLB at cyc 3 (event 1), and the ITLB requests a walk with V=0 at cyc 4 (event 2). The walker reads three PTEs from the root 0x8F00_0000, and the ITLB then answers the lookup with a hit.

At cyc 3 (event 1), itlb_ifu_rsp_val is asserted with itlb_ifu_status 1 for ifu_itlb_vpn 0x80000. At cyc 4 (event 2), tb.itlb_l2t_req_val and tb.itlb_l2t_req_rdy are asserted with tb.itlb_l2t_vpn 0x80000 and tb.itlb_l2t_v 0. tb.ptw_mem_req_paddr is 0x8F00_0010 at cyc 7, 0x8F00_8000 at cyc 13 and 0x8F00_9000 at cyc 19. At cyc 25, tb.l2t_itlb_rsp_val is asserted with tb.l2t_itlb_status 0 and tb.l2t_itlb_ppn 0x80000. At cyc 26, itlb_ifu_status is 0 with itlb_ifu_ppn 0x80000.

docs.title: 4.2 Svadu A-bit update
docs.text:
The walk for page C starts at cyc 46 (event 3). The leaf PTE of page C is valid and permitted, with A clear. With ADUE set, the walker's leaf evaluation requests an update instead of raising a page fault.3 In a single-stage walk, the update issues one compare-and-swap, at cyc 67 (event 4), whose compare value is the PTE read and whose swap value is the PTE with A set.4 The walk answers at cyc 73 (event 5).

At cyc 46 (event 3), the walk starts with tb.itlb_l2t_vpn 0x80010 and tb.itlb_l2t_v 0. At cyc 61, the walker reads the leaf at 0x8F00_9080. At cyc 67 (event 4), tb.ptw_mem_req_op is 1, with tb.ptw_mem_req_paddr 0x8F00_9080, tb.ptw_mem_req_cmp 0x2040_008B and tb.ptw_mem_req_swap 0x2040_00CB. The two values differ in bit 6, the A bit. At cyc 73 (event 5), tb.l2t_itlb_rsp_val is asserted with tb.l2t_itlb_status 0 and tb.l2t_itlb_ppn 0x81000.

docs.title: 4.3 Nested walk
docs.text:
With V=1 and hgatp not Bare, the walker enables the G-stage.5 Every VS-stage PTE address is a guest physical address, translated through the G-stage before the PTE is read, and the final guest physical address is translated the same way.

The walk for page V, which starts at cyc 170 (event 9), therefore makes 15 memory reads: three VS-stage PTEs, each preceded by a 3-level G-stage translation of its address, and a 3-level G-stage translation of the final guest physical address. The VS-stage leaf is read at cyc 246 (event 10), and the walk answers at cyc 267 (event 11). The figure below shows the reads.

The run has two walks with V=1. The first, at cyc 91 (event 6), is on the wrong path. The fetch has continued past the ecall, and when the ecall retires, a younger fetch on page C is translated with V=1. The backend's trap redirect at cyc 92 (event 7) flushes the block. Page C is not mapped in the VS-stage, so that walk ends with a fault at cyc 168 (event 8) that nothing delivers.6 This walk occupies the walker until then, so the walk for page V starts at cyc 170 (event 9). The first walk has 9 G-stage evaluations and the second has 12.

At cyc 91 (event 6), tb.itlb_l2t_req_val and tb.itlb_l2t_req_rdy are asserted with tb.itlb_l2t_vpn 0x80010 and tb.itlb_l2t_v 1. At cyc 92 (event 7), tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val is asserted with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc 0x8005_0000. At cyc 168 (event 8), tb.l2t_itlb_rsp_val is asserted with tb.l2t_itlb_status 1 and tb.l2t_itlb_cause 12.

At cyc 170 (event 9), the walk for page V starts with tb.itlb_l2t_vpn 0x80050 and tb.itlb_l2t_v 1, and tb.u_ptw.r_g_on is 1. At cyc 246 (event 10), tb.mem_ptw_rsp_val is asserted with tb.mem_ptw_rsp_data 0x0401_40CB: the VS-stage leaf, giving the guest physical address 0x1005_0000. At cyc 267 (event 11), tb.l2t_itlb_rsp_val is asserted with tb.l2t_itlb_status 0 and tb.l2t_itlb_ppn 0x81600.

docs.title: fd15_faults: Page, Access and Guest-Page Fetch Faults
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd15_faults (FD-15) demonstrates the three fault types reported by instruction fetch, and their propagation to decode:

  1. an instruction page fault, due to an unmapped page
  2. an instruction access fault, due to a mapped page whose physical page physical memory protection (PMP) denies execute
  3. an instruction guest-page fault, due to a guest physical page with no second-stage translation

The program makes three indirect jumps to targets that fault. The first two execute in supervisor mode under single-stage translation. An ecall then transfers execution to a guest under two-stage translation, for the third.

Each fault is recorded with its prediction block in the IFU, and is reported in the fault fields of the per-instruction packet, ifu_pd_pkt_t, sent to decode via the IBUF. The backend then redirects to the handler.

The result line in the log file reports the faults that reach decode with the expected cause and virtual address.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd15 in programs/fd15_faults.svh.

The code consists of a short prologue at the reset vector, then three indirect jumps to targets that fault. The handler of the first fault contains the second jump. The handler of the second fault executes an ecall to page V, which contains the third jump. The table gives each target and the listing gives the code.

The program first executes in S-mode under satp Sv39. PMP entry 0 is a 4 KiB NAPOT region at 0x8140_0000 with read and write permission and no execute, and PMP entry 2 grants read, write and execute everywhere. Entry 0 matches first.

Target Translation Fault Handler 0x8040_0010 nothing mapped page 0x8002_0000 0x8060_0010 leaf to 0x8140_0000, denied execute by PMP entry 0 access 0x8002_0040 0x8080_0010 VS-stage leaf to GPA 0x2000_0000, no G-stage mapping guest-page 0x8005_1000 
Address      Label  Instruction             Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0008         jal    x0, C            ; to page C

0x8001_0000  C:     c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8001_0006  J0:    jalr   x0, 0(x7)        ; to 0x8040_0010, page fault

0x8002_0000  H:     c.addi a0, 1            ; handler of the page fault
0x8002_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8002_0006  J1:    jalr   x0, 0(x7)        ; to 0x8060_0010, access fault

0x8002_0040  H1:    c.addi a0, 1            ; handler of the access fault
0x8002_0042         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8002_0046         ecall                   ; to VS-mode at V

0x8005_0000  V:     c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8005_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8005_0006  J2:    jalr   x0, 0(x7)        ; to 0x8080_0010, guest-page fault

0x8005_1000  V1:    c.addi a0, 1            ; handler of the guest-page fault
0x8005_1002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8005_1006         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8005_1008         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8005_100A  hold:  jal    x0, hold         ; termination

The three targets contain no code, because their fetches fault. The testbench compares the fault reported at decode with the expected cause and address. It also applies the change to guest execution when the ecall retires, in place of the trap to machine mode and the return that software would execute.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the control transfers.

The directions and targets are chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in them. x7 is never read.

The run has no accepted p2 slot groups, because no block repeats and the FTB therefore never hits.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows each faulting fetch. Sections 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3 describe how each fault arises, and section 4.4 describes the path that all three take to decode. fd14_translation section 4 defines the RISC-V translation terms.

Each jalr is mispredicted at its first execution, because no target is known, so the backend redirects to the target, and the fetch of the target then faults.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform. A signal the testbench drives, such as tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val, changes one time unit after the clock edge, so the waveform first shows the new value at the marker of the next cycle.

The waveform group itlb contains the IFU lookups, walker the walks, ifu_xlate the translation queue, ifu_fault the fault report to the FTQ, decode lane 0 at decode, and backend the redirects.

docs.title: 4.1 Instruction page fault
docs.text:
The walk for page 0x8040_0000 starts at cyc 90 (event 1) and answers a fault at cyc 104 (event 2), because nothing is mapped. The ITLB does not install a fault. It holds the fault in its tracker and answers the re-request with it.1 A later lookup of the page therefore walks again, which it does at cyc 107.

At cyc 90 (event 1), tb.itlb_l2t_req_val and tb.itlb_l2t_req_rdy are asserted with tb.itlb_l2t_vpn 0x80400 and tb.itlb_l2t_v 0. At cyc 104 (event 2), tb.l2t_itlb_rsp_val is asserted with tb.l2t_itlb_status 1 and tb.l2t_itlb_cause 12.

docs.title: 4.2 Instruction access fault
docs.text:
The walk for page 0x8060_0000 starts at cyc 166 (event 5) and answers a hit at cyc 187 (event 6), because the page has a valid leaf. The ITLB checks every translation against PMP and PMA for execute access at the effective privilege, and answers a hit that fails as a fault with the access cause, at cyc 188 (event 7).2 PMP entry 0 matches the physical page and has execute clear.

At cyc 187 (event 6), tb.l2t_itlb_rsp_val is asserted with tb.l2t_itlb_status 0 and tb.l2t_itlb_ppn 0x81400. At cyc 188 (event 7), itlb_ifu_rsp_val is asserted with itlb_ifu_status 2 and itlb_ifu_cause 1.

docs.title: 4.3 Instruction guest-page fault
docs.text:
The ecall's trap redirect to V is at cyc 202 (event 9). As in fd14, a younger fetch on the wrong path is translated with V=1 first: the walk for page H starts at cyc 201 and answers a fault at cyc 278 that nothing delivers. The walk for page V then runs from cyc 280 to 377.

The walk for page 0x8080_0000 starts at cyc 399 (event 10). The VS-stage leaf gives the guest physical address 0x2000_0000, which the G-stage does not map. A G-stage page fault is a guest-page fault, so the walker answers cause 20 at cyc 490 (event 11).3 The ITLB handles it as in section 4.1, and the page is walked again at cyc 493.

At cyc 399 (event 10), tb.itlb_l2t_req_val and tb.itlb_l2t_req_rdy are asserted with tb.itlb_l2t_vpn 0x80800 and tb.itlb_l2t_v 1. At cyc 490 (event 11), tb.l2t_itlb_rsp_val is asserted with tb.l2t_itlb_status 1 and tb.l2t_itlb_cause 20.

docs.title: 4.4 Fault propagation to decode
docs.text:
All three faults take the same path, with the same timing from the walker's answer. The translation queue records the page's fault, ifu_fetch requests no line on a faulting page, and F3 assigns each position its fault, cause and virtual address and writes them into the packet.4

Fault Walker answers ITLB answers Queue entry faulted Decode Trap redirect page 104 105 106 108 110 access 187 188 189 191 193 guest-page 490 491 492 494 496

At cyc 108 (event 3), tb.pd_out.[0].valid is asserted with tb.pd_out.[0].start_pc and tb.pd_out.[0].fault_va 0x8040_0010 and tb.pd_out.[0].fault_cause IFU_FAULT_PAGE. At cyc 110 (event 4), tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val is asserted with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_cause RC_TRAP and tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc 0x8002_0000.

At cyc 191 (event 8), tb.pd_out.[0].start_pc and tb.pd_out.[0].fault_va are 0x8060_0010, with tb.pd_out.[0].fault_cause IFU_FAULT_ACCESS.

At cyc 494 (event 12), tb.pd_out.[0].start_pc and tb.pd_out.[0].fault_va are 0x8080_0010, with tb.pd_out.[0].fault_cause IFU_FAULT_GUEST_PAGE and tb.pd_out.[0].fault_gpa 0x2000_0010.

docs.title: FD-16 Fetch Block Crossing a Page
fd16_page_cross: A Prediction Block Crossing a Page
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd16_page_cross (FD-16) demonstrates a prediction block that crosses a 4 KiB page boundary:

  1. the block is translated twice, once for each page
  2. the IFU requests one L1I line from each of two non-adjacent physical pages
  3. a 32-bit instruction straddling the boundary reaches decode whole

The program jumps to an address 16 bytes before the end of a page whose virtual successor is mapped to a non-adjacent physical page. The prediction block that starts there covers both pages.

The result line in the log file reports the number of blocks translated twice.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

docs.title: 1.1 Files
docs.text:

View the waveform (runs simulation first if FST is not up to date): 

make -C examples/fe_demo view S=fd16_page_cross

Console output: 

-I: fd16_page_cross : PASS : cyc = 112

Log file output: 

-I: fd16_page_cross: PASS, blocks translated twice 1, events checked 8 of 8,
    cyc 112

The testbench monitor, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh, supplies the count in the log line, while the expected instruction stream has not fully retired. The program has one crossing block, with PPNs 0x81000 and 0x81205.

Item Counter Counted blocks translated twice n_xq_cross u_ifu.u_xlate.xq_val, xq_pop and xq_cross, with xq_ppn0 not equal to xq_ppn1

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd16 in programs/fd16_page_cross.svh.

The code consists of a short prologue at the reset vector, a jump to 16 bytes before the end of page B, seven 16-bit instructions, a 32-bit instruction that straddles the page boundary, and a short epilogue.

The program runs in S-mode under satp Sv39. The two pages of the crossing block are adjacent in virtual addresses but not in physical addresses.

Page Virtual address Physical address reset 0x8000_0000 0x8000_0000 B 0x8001_0000 0x8100_0000 B+1 0x8001_1000 0x8120_5000 
Address      Label  Instruction             Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0008         jal    x0, S            ; to the crossing block

0x8001_0FF0  S:     c.addi a0, 1            ; 16 bytes before the page end
0x8001_0FF2         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_0FF4         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_0FF6         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_0FF8         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_0FFA         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_0FFC         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_0FFE  X:     addi   t0, t0, 1        ; straddles the page boundary

0x8001_1002         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8001_1004         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8001_1008         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8001_100A         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8001_100C         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8001_1010         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8001_1012         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8001_1014         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8001_1018  hold:  jal    x0, hold         ; termination

The two halfwords of the instruction at X are in different physical pages, at 0x8100_0FFE and 0x8120_5000.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work, other than the instruction at X. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to place X on the page boundary.

The run has no accepted p2 slot groups, because no block repeats and the FTB therefore never hits.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows the crossing block. Section 4.1 describes its two translations, section 4.2 its two line requests, and section 4.3 the instruction that straddles the boundary. fd14_translation section 4 defines the RISC-V translation terms.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

The waveform group ifu_xlate contains the translation queue, itlb the lookups, ifu_l1i the line requests, and decode lanes 0 and 7 at decode.

The figure below shows the block's layout.

docs.title: 4.1 Two translations
docs.text:
ifu_xlate marks a block as crossing when its start address has a page offset of at least 0xFE0, 32 bytes from the end of the page, and then requires two lookups.1 The block at 0x8001_0FF0 has page offset 0xFF0. Both lookups miss the ITLB, so each page is walked, from cyc 46 (event 1) and cyc 70 (event 2). The queue entry holds both results.

At cyc 46 (event 1), tb.itlb_l2t_req_val and tb.itlb_l2t_req_rdy are asserted with tb.itlb_l2t_vpn 0x80010, and the walk answers tb.l2t_itlb_ppn 0x81000 at cyc 67. At cyc 70 (event 2), tb.itlb_l2t_vpn is 0x80011, and the walk answers tb.l2t_itlb_ppn 0x81205 at cyc 91.

At cyc 94 (event 4), u_ifu.u_xlate.xq_val and u_ifu.u_xlate.xq_pop are asserted with u_ifu.u_xlate.xq_pc 0x8001_0FF0, u_ifu.u_xlate.xq_cross 1, u_ifu.u_xlate.xq_ppn0 0x81000 and u_ifu.u_xlate.xq_ppn1 0x81205.

docs.title: 4.2 Two line requests
docs.text:
A block that starts in the upper half of a line requires a second line. For a crossing block, that line is the first line of the second page.2

At cyc 93 (event 3), ifu_l1i_req_val and ifu_l1i_req_rdy are asserted with ifu_l1i_req_paddr 0x8100_0FC0. At cyc 94 (event 4), ifu_l1i_req_paddr is 0x8120_5000.

docs.title: 4.3 The straddling instruction
docs.text:
The instruction at X has its first halfword in the first line and its second halfword in the second line. Both lines miss in the L1I, so it cannot be assembled until the second line returns, at cyc 107 (event 5). Decode receives it whole at cyc 109 (event 6), as the last of the eight instructions of that bundle.

At cyc 105, l1i_ifu_rsp_val is asserted with l1i_ifu_rsp_id 0, the first line. At cyc 107 (event 5), l1i_ifu_rsp_val is asserted with l1i_ifu_rsp_id 1, the second line.

At cyc 109 (event 6), tb.pd_out.[7].valid is asserted with tb.pd_out.[7].start_pc 0x8001_0FFE, tb.pd_out.[7].pos 7, tb.pd_out.[7].instr 0x0012_8293 and tb.pd_out.[7].is_rvc 0. At cyc 110, tb.pd_out.[0].start_pc is 0x8001_1002, the next instruction.

docs.title: fd17_rvc: Compressed and Unaligned Code
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd17_rvc (FD-17) demonstrates compressed and non-aligned code:

  1. a 32-bit instruction at the last halfword of a block reaches decode whole
  2. the next block starts on the tail of that instruction
  3. compressed control transfers reach decode expanded, and the blocks they start are not 32-byte aligned

The program runs mixed 16-bit and 32-bit instructions into the straddling instruction, then eight passes of a loop of compressed control transfers.

The result line in the log file reports the number of straddling instructions delivered whole and the number of 16-bit instructions.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

0x8000_003E  X:     addi   t0, t0, 1        ; straddles the block end

0x8000_0042         c.addi a0, 1            ; mixed code
0x8000_0044         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; mixed code
0x8000_0048         c.addi a0, 1            ; mixed code
0x8000_004A         c.addi a0, 1            ; mixed code
0x8000_004C         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; mixed code

0x8000_0050  top:   c.addi a0, 1            ; loop start
0x8000_0052         c.bnez x8, T            ; taken on odd passes
0x8000_0054         c.addi a0, 1            ; reached on even passes
0x8000_0056  T:     addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8000_005A         c.jalr x1               ; call to fn
0x8000_005C  R:     c.addi a0, 1            ; return address
0x8000_005E         c.j    U                ; to U
0x8000_0066  U:     c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8000_0068         c.beqz x8, top          ; taken on passes 0 to 6

0x8000_006A         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_006C         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8000_0070         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_0072  hold:  jal    x0, hold         ; termination

0x8000_0400  fn:    c.addi a0, 1            ; function body
0x8000_0402         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; function body

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work, other than the instruction at X. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to place X and the control transfers.

The directions and targets are chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in them. x8 is never read.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows the three behaviors of the introduction. Section 4.1 describes the straddling instruction, section 4.2 the expansion of the compressed control transfers, and section 4.3 the blocks those transfers start.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

The waveform group ftq_ifu contains the blocks, ifu_f3 the predecode writeback, ifu_f3_straddle the straddle register, ibuf the offers to the instruction buffer, backend the backend redirects, and decode the lanes at decode.

The figure below shows the two blocks around the block end.

docs.title: 4.1 The straddling instruction
docs.text:
The IFU selects 17 halfwords from the block offset, so a 32-bit instruction that starts at position 15 of a 32-byte block completes inside that block.1 The block at 0x8000_0020 starts in the upper half of its line, so it also uses the next line, which holds the second halfword of X.2

That block ends by falling through, and its last instruction starts 2 bytes before the end of the block. The straddle register therefore records the next block's start address, and the next block begins after the tail.3

At cyc 20, ifu_ibuf_en is 0xFBBB, with bit 15 set for X. At cyc 21, it is 0xEF76 for the block at 0x8000_0040, with bit 0 clear for the tail.

At cyc 21 (event 1), tb.pd_out.[4].valid is asserted with tb.pd_out.[4].start_pc 0x8000_003E, tb.pd_out.[4].pos 15, tb.pd_out.[4].instr 0x0012_8293 and tb.pd_out.[4].is_rvc 0. u_ifu.u_f3.r_strad_val is asserted with u_ifu.u_f3.r_strad_pc 0x8000_0040.

At cyc 22 (event 2), tb.pd_out.[0].start_pc is 0x8000_0042 and tb.pd_out.[0].pos is 1, with tb.pd_out.[0].ftq_idx 2, the next block.

docs.title: 4.2 Compressed control transfers
docs.text:
Each compressed control transfer reaches decode as its 32-bit expansion, with is_rvc 1.

Instruction cyc Lane Address instr Expansion c.jalr x1 23 1 0x8000_005A 0x0000_80E7 jalr x1, 0(x1) c.jr x1 95 2 0x8000_0406 0x0000_8067 jalr x0, 0(x1) c.j U 96 1 0x8000_005E 0x0080_006F jal x0, +8 c.beqz x8 97 1 0x8000_0068 0xFE04_04E3 beq x8, x0, -24 c.bnez x8 98 1 0x8000_0052 0x0004_1263 bne x8, x0, +4

docs.title: 4.3 Non-aligned block starts
docs.text:
A taken transfer starts the next block at its target, so the loop's blocks start at 0x8000_0050, 0x8000_0056, 0x8000_005C, 0x8000_0066 and 0x8000_0054. Positions are counted from the block start.

The first pass has no predictions, so each transfer is corrected by a redirect.

The c.jalr is resolved by the backend: tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val is asserted with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc 0x8000_0400 at cyc 25. At cyc 28 (event 3), ftq_ifu_start_pc is 0x8000_0400. The predecode redirect to 0x8000_0066 at cyc 22 is for the c.j, which follows the c.jalr, and is on the wrong path.

The c.jr is also resolved by the backend, with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc 0x8000_005C at cyc 45. At cyc 48 (event 4), ftq_ifu_start_pc is 0x8000_005C, the first block with a non-aligned start, and ftq_ifu_next_pc is 0x8000_007C. At cyc 53, tb.pd_out.[0].start_pc is 0x8000_005C with tb.pd_out.[0].pos 0.

The c.j is corrected by predecode: u_ftq.w_pd_redir_val is asserted at cyc 54. At cyc 57 (event 5), ftq_ifu_start_pc is 0x8000_0066.

The c.beqz is resolved by the backend, with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc 0x8000_0050 at cyc 65. At cyc 69 (event 6), ftq_ifu_start_pc is 0x8000_0050.

Compressed transfers are predicted in later passes. At cyc 90 (event 7), ftq_ifu_start_pc is 0x8000_0400 and ftq_ifu_next_pc is 0x8000_005C, with ftq_ifu_taken_val asserted and ftq_ifu_taken_pos 3, the position of the c.jr.

docs.title: fd18_uncached: Uncached Fetch
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd18_uncached (FD-18) demonstrates fetch from uncached pages:

  1. the IFU fetches one instruction per FTQ entry
  2. each entry is fetched only after every older entry has committed
  3. the L1I answers uncached requests from memory and does not fill the lines

The program runs from a page with PBMT NC, then from a page with PBMT IO.

The result line in the log file reports the uncached requests from each page and the number of uncached lines filled.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

docs.text:

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd18 in programs/fd18_uncached.svh.

The code consists of a short prologue, a cacheable page that jumps to the NC page, code on the NC page with branches, a loop and a function call, and code on the IO page with a taken branch.

The program runs in S-mode under satp Sv39.

Page Virtual address Physical address Type reset 0x8000_0000 0x8000_0000 cacheable c 0x8001_0000 0x8100_0000 cacheable u 0x8001_1000 0x8120_3000 PBMT 1, NC io 0x8001_2000 0x8120_4000 PBMT 2, IO 
Address      Label  Instruction             Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0008         jal    x0, C            ; to page c

0x8001_0000  C:     c.addi a0, 1            ; filler

0x8001_0006         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_0008         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler

0x8001_1010  U:     c.addi a0, 1            ; filler

0x8001_1202         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; loop body
0x8001_1206         bne    x6, x0, L        ; three passes
0x8001_120A         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_120C         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8001_1210         jal    x0, D            ; to page c

0x8001_0200  D:     c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_0202         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler

0x8001_2016         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_2018         bne    x6, x0, J        ; taken
0x8001_2022  J:     c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8001_2024         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler

0x8001_1400  fn:    c.addi a0, 1            ; function body

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the control transfers.

The directions and targets are chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in them. x6 is never read.

The modeled backend runs in eager mode for this program. It commits the entry of the last retired instruction without waiting for the next instruction, because the next instruction waits for that commit.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows an uncached instruction through fetch. Section 4.1 describes how a page is marked uncached, section 4.2 the fetch of one instruction, section 4.3 the requests by instruction, section 4.4 the control transfers, and section 4.5 the absence of L1I fills.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

The waveform group ifu_xlate contains the translation queue and the page attributes, ifu_f3 the end of each block, ifu_fetch the commit gate, ifu_l1i the requests, l1i the L1I and its memory requests, backend the commits and the redirects, and decode lane 0 at decode.

docs.title: 4.1 Uncached marking
docs.text:
On an ITLB hit, the translation queue marks a block uncached when its page is not both cacheable and idempotent.1 PBMT NC clears the cacheable attribute, and PBMT IO clears both.2

itlb_ifu_pma bit 0 is the cacheable attribute and bit 3 the idempotent attribute. It is 1111 for the cacheable page c at cyc 68, 1110 for the NC page at cyc 110, and 0110 for the IO page at cyc 646.

docs.title: 4.2 One instruction at a time
docs.text:
The IFU does not start an uncached block until ftq_ifu_commit_ptr equals its FTQ index.3 F3 then delivers only the first instruction of the block and ends the block there, so the FTQ redirects to the next instruction, which is a new entry.4

The table shows the instruction at 0x8001_1010, the first on the NC page.

cyc Event Reading 111 1 ifu_l1i_req_val and ifu_l1i_req_uncached asserted, ifu_l1i_req_paddr 0x8120_3000 112 u_l1i.b_mis_valid.[0] asserted 113 tb.l1i_mem_a_valid asserted, tb.l1i_mem_a_address 0x8120_3000 121 tb.l1i_mem_d_valid asserted, also at cyc 122 123 l1i_ifu_rsp_val asserted 125 tb.pd_out.[0].start_pc 0x8001_1010 126 2 ifu_ftq_uc_end and ifu_ftq_mis_val asserted, u_ftq.w_pd_redir_pc 0x8001_1012 128 tb.bkend_ftq_commit_idx 2 129 3 ftq_ifu_commit_ptr 3, u_ifu.u_fetch.w_uc_gate asserted, ftq_ifu_start_pc 0x8001_1012 130 the next request, ifu_l1i_req_paddr 0x8120_3000

The next instruction therefore starts 19 cycles after the previous one. The IO page behaves the same way: requests at cyc 647 (event 8) and 666.

docs.title: 4.3 Requests by instruction
docs.text:
An instruction in the lower half of a line requests that line alone. An instruction in the upper half also requests the next line.5 At cyc 193, ifu_l1i_req_paddr is 0x8120_3000 with ifu_l1i_req_id 0, and at cyc 194 it is 0x8120_3040 with ifu_l1i_req_id 1, for the instruction at 0x8001_1022.

The 28 requests from the NC page are for 24 instructions:

Addresses Instructions Requests First 0x8001_1010 to 0x8001_102E 9 14 cyc 111 (event 1) 0x8001_1200 to 0x8001_1210 12 11 cyc 306 (event 4) 0x8001_1400 to 0x8001_1406 3 3 cyc 555 (event 6)

The 10 requests from the IO page are for 7 instructions, the last at cyc 772 (event 9).

The loop has one instruction with no request. On the third pass, the block at 0x8001_1200 follows the predicted-taken bne with no redirect, and the previous request was for the same line. At cyc 427 (event 5), u_ifu.u_fetch.w_reuse0 is asserted with no ifu_l1i_req_val, and tb.pd_out.[0].start_pc is 0x8001_1200 at cyc 429.6

docs.title: 4.4 Control transfers
docs.text:
A conditional branch ends its block like any other instruction, at the sequential address. At cyc 183, u_ftq.w_pd_redir_pc is 0x8001_101C for the bne at 0x8001_1018. The backend then corrects the path, with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc 0x8001_1022 at cyc 189.

A jal redirects at predecode to its target. At cyc 298, ifu_ftq_mis_val is asserted without ifu_ftq_uc_end, and u_ftq.w_pd_redir_pc is 0x8001_1200.

A ret is delivered alone with no predecode redirect, because only the backend knows its target. At cyc 608 (event 7), ifu_ftq_pdwb_val is asserted with ifu_ftq_mis_val and ifu_ftq_uc_end clear, and tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc is 0x8001_020C at cyc 611.

docs.title: 4.5 No L1I fills
docs.text: An uncached access is a miss whatever the tags hold, and the MSHR register it takes is marked not to allocate.7 At cyc 316 and 317, tb.l1i_mem_d_valid is asserted for the line at 0x8120_3200 with u_l1i.u_mshr.b_fil_valid clear. Fills in this run are for the cacheable pages, for example from cyc 38 for the reset page.

docs.title: fd19_fencei_cbo: FENCE.I and cbo.inval
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd19_fencei_cbo (FD-19) demonstrates the two instruction cache maintenance operations. A FENCE.I invalidates every L1I line, and a cbo.inval invalidates one line. For each operation, the backend, the IFU and the L1I complete a handshake, fetch restarts at the next instruction, and the modified code then runs.

The program calls a function, rewrites it with a store, and calls it again after a FENCE.I. A second function repeats this with a cbo.inval of its line.

The result line in the log file reports the invalidates of each kind, the completions, the acknowledgments and the restarts.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

make -C examples/fe_demo view S=fd19_fencei_cbo

Log file output:

    invalidates done 2, maintenance acknowledgments 2,
    restarts at the next instruction 2, events checked 17 of 17, cyc 235

The testbench monitor, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh, supplies the counts in the log line.

Item Counter Counted whole-cache invalidates n_inv_all ifu_l1i_inv_val, ifu_l1i_inv_rdy and ifu_l1i_inv_all line invalidates n_inv_line ifu_l1i_inv_val and ifu_l1i_inv_rdy, with ifu_l1i_inv_all clear invalidates done n_inv_done l1i_ifu_inv_done maintenance acknowledgments n_mt_ack ifu_cmt_maint_ack restarts at the next instruction n_restart the first block after an acknowledgment starts at the address after the maintenance instruction

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd19 in programs/fd19_fencei_cbo.svh.

The code consists of two calls of a function f, a store that rewrites f, a FENCE.I, and a third call of f. The same sequence follows for a function g, with a cbo.inval of its line, then a short epilogue.

The program runs in M-mode with bare addressing.

Address      Label  Instruction             Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0008         jal    x1, f            ; first call of f
0x8000_000C         jal    x1, f            ; second call of f
0x8000_0010         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8000_0012         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8000_0016         sw     x0, 0(a0)        ; rewrites f
0x8000_001A         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8000_001C         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8000_0020         fence.i                 ; invalidates every line
0x8000_0024         c.addi a0, 1            ; next instruction
0x8000_0026         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8000_002A         jal    x1, f            ; runs the new body of f

0x8000_002E         c.addi a0, 1            ; filler
0x8000_0030         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; filler
0x8000_0034         jal    x1, g            ; first call of g
0x8000_0038         jal    x1, g            ; second call of g
0x8000_003C         sw     x0, 0(a0)        ; rewrites g
0x8000_0040         bne    x6, x0, M        ; taken
0x8000_0046  M:     cbo.inval (a0)          ; invalidates the line of g
0x8000_004A         mixed code              ; next instruction, 60 instructions
0x8000_00EA         jal    x1, g            ; runs the new body of g

0x8000_00EE         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_00F0         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8000_00F4  hold:  jal    x0, hold         ; termination

0x8000_0800  f:     c.addi a0, 1            ; six in the old body, to 0x080A
0x8000_080C         ret                     ; return

0x8000_0C40  g:     c.addi a0, 1            ; six in the old body, to 0x0C4A
0x8000_0C4C         ret                     ; return

The new bodies of f and g are three addi t1, t1, 1 and the same ret.

The cbo.inval names physical address 0x8000_0C64, in the line of g at 0x8000_0C40.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the operations.

A store's rewrite takes effect when the store retires, so memory holds the old body until then. The directions and targets are chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in them.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows the two maintenance operations. Section 4.1 describes their handshake, section 4.2 the drain, and section 4.3 the effect of each invalidate.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

The waveform group maintenance contains the handshake, backend the redirects, ftq_ifu the blocks, ifu_l1i the line requests and memory requests, and decode lane 0 at decode.

docs.title: 4.1 The maintenance handshake
docs.text:
When a maintenance instruction retires, the backend stops taking decode's output and requests the operation.1 The IFU passes the invalidate to the L1I.2 The L1I takes no new request, drains, clears the lines and signals done.3 The IFU clears its line buffer and acknowledges, and the backend redirects to the next instruction.

The FENCE.I clears every set. The cbo.inval clears every way of the set of the named line.4

Step FENCE.I cbo.inval tb.cmt_ifu_maint_val asserted, tb.cmt_ifu_maint_op cyc 71, op 0 cyc 184, op 1 the L1I takes the invalidate, ifu_l1i_inv_val and ifu_l1i_inv_rdy cyc 71 (event 1) cyc 184 (event 9) u_l1i.u_maint.r_st 1, M_DRAIN cyc 72 cyc 185 u_l1i.u_maint.r_st 2, M_CLEAR cyc 73 cyc 186 l1i_ifu_inv_done cyc 74 (event 2) cyc 187 (event 10) tb.ifu_cmt_maint_ack cyc 75 (event 3) cyc 188 (event 11) tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val, tb.bkend_ftq_redir_cause 2, RC_REPLAY cyc 77 (event 4) cyc 190 (event 12) tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc 0x8000_0024 0x8000_004A ftq_ifu_start_pc at the next instruction cyc 79 (event 5) cyc 192 (event 13)

ifu_l1i_inv_all is 1 at cyc 71. At cyc 184 it is 0, and ifu_l1i_inv_paddr is 0x8000_0C64.

The bne before the cbo.inval is taken and not predicted. tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc is 0x8000_0046 at cyc 174 (event 8), with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_cause 0.

docs.title: 4.2 The drain
docs.text:
The FENCE.I waits until no MSHR register is in use, and the cbo.inval waits until no register holds the named line.5 Neither waits in this run, so M_DRAIN lasts one cycle both times.

u_l1i.mt_busy_any is 0 at cyc 71. At cyc 184, u_l1i.mt_busy_any is 1 and u_l1i.mt_busy_line is 0.

docs.title: 4.3 The effect of each invalidate
docs.text:
The FENCE.I clears every line, so later requests miss. tb.l1i_mem_a_valid is asserted with tb.l1i_mem_a_address 0x8000_0800 at cyc 77 and 0x8000_0000 at cyc 82 (event 6). The line at 0x8000_0000 had been requested from memory at cyc 6.

At cyc 58, tb.pd_out.[0].start_pc is 0x8000_0800 with tb.pd_out.[0].instr 0x0015_0513, the old body of f. At cyc 106 (event 7), it is 0x8000_0800 with tb.pd_out.[0].instr 0x0013_0313, the new body.

The cbo.inval clears only the set of its line. At cyc 208, ifu_l1i_req_paddr is 0x8000_0C40, and at cyc 210 (event 14) tb.l1i_mem_a_address is 0x8000_0C40. At cyc 209, ifu_l1i_req_paddr is 0x8000_0000 with no memory request.

At cyc 159, tb.pd_out.[0].start_pc is 0x8000_0C40 with tb.pd_out.[0].instr 0x0015_0513, the old body of g. At cyc 222 (event 15), it is 0x8000_0C40 with tb.pd_out.[0].instr 0x0013_0313, the new body.

docs.title: fd20_backpressure: Backpressure
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd20_backpressure (FD-20) demonstrates a stall propagating from decode back to the p0 request. Decode holds its bundle, the instruction buffer fills and stalls the IFU, the IFU stalls the FTQ, the FTQ fills, and the FTQ withholds the p0 request.

The program runs a 40-pass loop with the backend taking decode's output one cycle in four.

The result line in the log file reports the stall cycles at each point.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

docs.title: 1.1 Files
docs.text:
DEMO=$RVA_ROOT/examples/fe_demo

File Path This file $DEMO/docs/fd20_backpressure.md Program (stimulus) $DEMO/programs/fd20_backpressure.svh Surfer sucl $DEMO/waves/fd20_backpressure.sucl Log $DEMO/out/fd20_backpressure/fd20_backpressure.log Waveform $DEMO/out/fd20_backpressure/fd20_backpressure.fst Waveform (online) Link Block connectivity $DEMO/docs/fe_block.svg Pipeline view $DEMO/docs/fe_pipe.svg Common description $DEMO/docs/demo_explainer.md

docs.title: 2. Run the scenario
docs.text:
Run simulation: 

make -C examples/fe_demo fd20_backpressure

View the waveform (runs simulation first if FST is not up to date): 

make -C examples/fe_demo view S=fd20_backpressure

Console output: 

-I: fd20_backpressure : PASS : cyc = 537

Log file output: 

-I: fd20_backpressure: PASS, stall cycles with the instruction buffer full 378,
    FTQ full 324, decode held 368, no p0 request 331, events checked 8 of 8,
    cyc 537

The testbench monitor, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh, supplies the counts in the log line. They are counts of cycles, not of stall events. n_p0_held counts every hold of the p0 request, so it includes FTB update holds as well as ftq_full.

Item Counter Counted instruction buffer full n_ibuf_full ifu_ibuf_val with ibuf_ifu_rdy low FTQ full n_ftq_full ftq_full decode held n_dec_stall tb.pd_out.[0].valid with tb.dec_ibuf_rdy low no p0 request n_p0_held ftq_pred_val_p0 low

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd20 in programs/fd20_backpressure.svh.

The code consists of a short prologue, a loop of 23 mixed instructions and a back edge that runs for 40 passes, and a short epilogue.

The program runs in M-mode with bare addressing.

Address      Label  Instruction             Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue

0x8000_0008  top:   mixed code              ; 23 instructions, to 0x8000_0045
0x8000_0046         bne    x6, x0, top      ; taken on passes 0 to 38

0x8000_004A         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_004C         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8000_0050         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_0052  hold:  jal    x0, hold         ; termination

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to fill the loop.

The direction of the back edge is chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in it. x6 is never read.

The modeled backend takes decode's output one cycle in four, set by be_rdy_pat in the program.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows the stall from decode back to the p0 request, one section for each point. Section 4.5 describes the recovery.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

The waveform group decode contains the bundle, ibuf the instruction buffer, ftq_ifu the blocks and the line buffer, ftq the FTQ occupancy, and bp_cluster_p0 the p0 request and its holds.

The figure below shows the occupancy of the instruction buffer and the FTQ.

docs.title: 4.1 Decode
docs.text: tb.dec_ibuf_rdy is high one cycle in four: at cyc 17, 21, 25 and so on. At cyc 18 (event 1), tb.pd_out.[0].valid is asserted with tb.dec_ibuf_rdy low, the first bundle held.

docs.title: 4.2 The instruction buffer
docs.text:
The instruction buffer takes a block only at 48 entries or fewer, out of 64.1 It takes more than decode removes: a block here offers 12 instructions, and decode takes 8 in one cycle of four. At cyc 73, u_ibuf.w_n_pres and u_ibuf.w_n_pop are 8.

u_ibuf.r_count is 40 at cyc 70, with ibuf_ifu_rdy asserted. At cyc 71 (event 2), it is 52, with ifu_ibuf_val asserted and ibuf_ifu_rdy low.

docs.title: 4.3 The IFU
docs.text:
F3 holds its block while ibuf_ifu_rdy is low.2 Blocks then stop leaving the IFU, and the 16 slots of its line buffer fill.

At cyc 86, ftq_ifu_req_rdy is asserted. At cyc 87 (event 3), ftq_ifu_req_val is asserted with ftq_ifu_req_rdy low and ftq_ifu_flush_val clear, and u_ifu.u_lbuf.w_slot_ok is 0: no slot is free for the next line.3 The earlier low cycles of ftq_ifu_req_rdy, at cyc 22, 31, 45 and 54, are flush cycles.

docs.title: 4.4 The FTQ and the p0 request
docs.text:
The FTQ keeps allocating while the IFU takes fewer blocks, so its occupancy rises until it reaches 64 entries.4 ftq_full then holds the p0 request.5

At cyc 138 (event 4), u_ftq.u_ptr.w_age_alloc is 64 and ftq_full is asserted, with ftq_pred_val_p0 low and u_ftq.u_npc.h2_ftq_full asserted. u_ftq.w_commit_ptr and ftq_pred_idx_p0 are both 16.

From then on, each commit allows one request. At cyc 144 (event 5), u_ftq.w_commit_ptr is 17, ftq_full is clear and ftq_pred_val_p0 is asserted. At cyc 145, ftq_full is asserted again.

The FTB update hold also withholds the p0 request.6 At cyc 82, 94 and 106, before the FTQ is full, u_ftq.u_npc.h3_ftb_upd is asserted with ftq_pred_val_p0 low and ftq_full clear.

docs.title: 4.5 Recovery
docs.text: The back edge of the last pass falls through, and the backend redirects to the epilogue. At cyc 526 (event 6), tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val is asserted with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc 0x8000_004A. The redirect clears the stall: ftq_full is clear, u_ibuf.r_count is 0 and u_ftq.u_ptr.w_age_alloc is 1.

docs.title: 5. Events
docs.text: # cyc Event Other 0 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests 0x8000_0000 the same cycle fast init 1 18 decode first holds a bundle: pd_out.[0].valid with dec_ibuf_rdy low decode stall 2 71 the instruction buffer first deasserts ready: ifu_ibuf_val with ibuf_ifu_rdy low, r_count 52 buffer full 3 87 the IFU first deasserts ready: ftq_ifu_req_val with ftq_ifu_req_rdy low, no flush no line buffer slot 4 138 the FTQ first full (ftq_full); the p0 request is withheld FTQ full 5 144 a commit clears ftq_full, and p0 issues one request full again at cyc 145 6 526 back edge falls through, a misprediction; redirect to 0x8000_004A pass 39, backend 7 537 the run ends

docs.title: 6. Waveform

docs.title: fd21_commit: Commit
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd21_commit (FD-21) demonstrates commit in the FTQ and the RAS. The backend's retirement watermark moves the FTQ commit pointer one entry per cycle, and each committed entry that ends in a call or a return pushes or pops the RAS commit stack.

The program runs six passes of a main function that calls f, with f calling g and then h.

The result line in the log file reports the cycles in which the commit pointer moved and the cycles in which the RAS commit stack changed.

This scenario runs in the 1-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=1.

Item Counter Counted the commit pointer moved n_commit_adv u_ftq.w_commit_ptr differs from the cycle before the RAS commit stack changed n_csp_chg u_bpu.u_ras.csp or u_bpu.u_ras.commit_top_addr differs from the cycle before

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd21 in programs/fd21_commit.svh.

The code consists of a short prologue, a loop in which main calls f and f calls g and then h, and a short epilogue.

The program runs in M-mode with bare addressing.

Address      Label  Instruction             Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1            ; prologue

0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1            ; ten, to 0x8000_001A
0x8000_001C         jal    x1, f            ; main calls f
0x8000_0020         c.addi a0, 1            ; return address
0x8000_0022         bne    x6, x0, top      ; taken on passes 0 to 4

0x8000_0026         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_0028         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; epilogue
0x8000_002C         c.addi a0, 1            ; epilogue
0x8000_002E  hold:  jal    x0, hold         ; termination

0x8000_0800  f:     c.addi a0, 1            ; function body
0x8000_0802         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; function body
0x8000_0806         c.addi a0, 1            ; function body
0x8000_0808         c.addi a0, 1            ; ten, to 0x8000_081A
0x8000_081C         jal    x1, g            ; f calls g
0x8000_0820         c.addi a0, 1            ; return address, 14, to 0x083A
0x8000_083C         jal    x1, h            ; f calls h
0x8000_0840         c.addi a0, 1            ; return address
0x8000_0842         ret                     ; f returns to main

0x8000_0A00  g:     c.addi a0, 1            ; function body
0x8000_0A02         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; function body
0x8000_0A06         ret                     ; g returns to f

0x8000_0C00  h:     c.addi a0, 1            ; function body
0x8000_0C02         addi   t0, t0, 1        ; function body
0x8000_0C06         ret                     ; h returns to f

Each pass makes three calls and three returns, and the deepest point is two return addresses.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to separate the control transfers.

The direction of the back edge is chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in it. x6 is never read.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows a commit from the backend to the RAS. Section 4.1 describes the watermark, section 4.2 the commit walk, section 4.3 the RAS commit stack, and section 4.4 the speculative stack.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

The waveform group backend contains the watermark, ftq the commit pointer and the walk, ras_commit the commit stack, and ras the speculative stack.

docs.title: 4.1 The watermark
docs.text:
The backend reports the newest FTQ entry whose instructions have all retired. That is known only when the first instruction of the next entry retires.1

The block at 0x8000_0800, entry 1, reaches decode at cyc 37. At cyc 40 (event 1), tb.bkend_ftq_commit_val is asserted with tb.bkend_ftq_commit_idx 0.

docs.title: 4.2 The commit walk
docs.text:
The FTQ frees the entries up to the watermark, one per cycle, because the RAS commit port takes one operation per cycle.2

At cyc 205 to 208 (event 8), u_ftq.w_commit_step_val is asserted with u_ftq.w_commit_ptr 38, 39, 40 and 41, toward tb.bkend_ftq_commit_idx 41. The pointer is 42 at cyc 209.

A restore suspends the walk.3 At cyc 145, u_ftq.u_commit.w_walk_stop is asserted with ftq_ifu_flush_val, and u_ftq.w_commit_step_val is clear for that cycle.

The figure below shows the watermark, the commit pointer and the commit stack from cyc 125. The watermark moves in steps, and the pointer follows it one entry per cycle. u_bpu.u_ras.csp repeats 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 0 on each pass.

docs.title: 4.3 The RAS commit stack
docs.text:
A committing entry that ends in a taken call or return raises ras_commit_val.4 A call pushes ras_commit_ret_addr, and a return pops. A return does not use ras_commit_ret_addr.5 u_bpu.u_ras.commit_top_addr is the entry below u_bpu.u_ras.csp.

cyc Event ras_commit_br_type u_bpu.u_ras.csp u_bpu.u_ras.commit_top_addr 40 1 DIRECT_CALL 0 41 2 1 0x8000_0020 61 DIRECT_CALL 1 0x8000_0020 62 3 RETURN 2 0x8000_0820 63 4 1 0x8000_0020

The walk at cyc 205 to 208 commits a call and two returns. u_bpu.u_ras.csp is 1 at cyc 205, 2 at cyc 206, 1 at cyc 207 and 0 at cyc 208.

The run has 36 RAS commits, 18 calls and 18 returns.

docs.title: 4.4 The speculative stack
docs.text:
The speculative pointers move ahead of the commit stack. u_bpu.u_ras.tosr and u_bpu.u_ras.tosw stay at 0 until cyc 124, and the first predicted-taken block follows at cyc 125.

At cyc 124 (event 5), u_bpu.u_ras.tosw is 2 and u_bpu.u_ras.csp is 0. The next call commits at cyc 134 (event 6), and u_bpu.u_ras.csp is 1 at cyc 135.

docs.title: 5. Events
docs.text: # cyc Event Other 0 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests 0x8000_0000 the same cycle fast init 1 40 first commit: watermark 0, the pointer steps, and the RAS commits the call to f return address 0x8000_0020 2 41 the commit stack reaches depth 1 (u_ras.csp), top 0x8000_0020 main 3 62 the commit stack reaches depth 2, and the first return commits top 0x8000_0820 4 63 the return has popped: depth 1, top 0x8000_0020 5 124 the speculative stack first moves: tosw 2, with csp 0 ahead of commit 6 134 the next call commits csp 1 at cyc 135 7 204 back edge falls through, a misprediction; redirect to 0x8000_0026 pass 5, backend 8 205 the walk commits four entries in four consecutive cycles, to watermark 41 cyc 205 to 208 9 214 the run ends

docs.title: fd22_sc_slot1: SC Reversing Slot 1
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd22_sc_slot1 (FD-22) demonstrates the statistical corrector (SC) reversing the second of two conditional branches in one prediction block. TAGE predicts both branches at p2, one in each prediction slot. At p3, SC reverses the direction of the branch in slot 1, and the cluster redirects the request stream. fd05_p3_override shows the same reversal in slot 0.

The program runs a 48-pass loop whose first block holds two conditional branches: A, never taken, and B, taken on odd passes.

The result line in the log file reports the p3 redirects from each slot that SC reversed.

This scenario runs in the 2-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=2.

The testbench monitor, tb/fe_demo_mon.svh, supplies the counts in the log line. It counts a p3 redirect that the FTQ accepted, u_ftq.w_ok_redir_p3, for the block at p3.

Item Counter Counted from slot 1, SC, behind TAGE n_sc_s1 slot 1 raises the redirect, slot 1 is a conditional with pred_src PRED_SC, and slot 0 is a conditional with pred_src PRED_TAGE from slot 0, SC n_sc_s0 slot 0 raises the redirect, with pred_src PRED_SC

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd22 in programs/fd22_sc_slot1.svh.

The code consists of a short prologue, a loop of 48 passes, and a short epilogue. The first block of the loop holds two conditional branches: A, never taken, and B, taken on the odd passes.

The program runs in M-mode with bare addressing.

Address      Label  Instruction              Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1             ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1             ; prologue

0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1             ; filler
0x8000_000A         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; filler
0x8000_000E  A:     bne    x6, x0, 0x8000_0014 ; never taken
0x8000_0012         c.addi a0, 1             ; always executed
0x8000_0014         c.addi a0, 1             ; filler
0x8000_0016  B:     bne    x6, x0, 0x8000_001C ; taken on odd passes
0x8000_001A         c.addi a0, 1             ; executed when B is not taken
0x8000_001C         c.addi a0, 1             ; target of B
0x8000_001E         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; filler
0x8000_0022         c.addi a0, 1             ; filler
0x8000_0024         c.addi a0, 1             ; filler
0x8000_0026         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; filler
0x8000_002A         c.addi a0, 1             ; filler
0x8000_002C         bne    x6, x0, top       ; back edge

0x8000_0030         c.addi a0, 1             ; epilogue
0x8000_0032         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; epilogue
0x8000_0036         c.addi a0, 1             ; epilogue
0x8000_0038  hold:  jal    x0, hold          ; termination

In the block at top, A is at halfword position 3 and B at position 7. The filler after B moves the back edge into the next block, so the block at top holds exactly the two conditional branches. The target of B lies inside the block, so the successor of the block differs between B taken and B not taken.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to place the branches.

The directions and targets are chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in them. x6 is never read.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows the block at top. Section 4.1 describes the two branches at p2, section 4.2 the SC response at p3, and section 4.3 the reversals in the run.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

The waveform group tage_p2 contains the TAGE response, bp_cluster_p2 the p2 group, sc_p3 the SC response, bp_cluster_p3 the p3 group and redirects, ftq the accepted groups, and backend the backend redirects.

The figure below shows the block and its two successors.

docs.title: 4.1 Two conditional branches in one prediction block
docs.text:
The FTB records up to NUM_PRED_SLOTS branches for a block start address, each with its position.1 In the 2-prediction slot configuration, the block at top has A in slot 0 and B in slot 1. For each conditional branch, the direction comes from TAGE when TAGE answers for the block, and the pred_src of the slot is then PRED_TAGE.2

At cyc 45 (event 2), u_bpu.r_pc_p2 is 0x8000_0008, bpu_slot_p2.[0].pos is 3 and bpu_slot_p2.[1].pos is 7. Both slots have br_type COND and pred_src PRED_TAGE. A is predicted not taken and B taken.

docs.title: 4.2 SC answers at p3 for each slot
docs.text:
SC answers one cycle after TAGE, at p3, separately for each slot. For a conditional branch with an SC response and no loop predictor direction, the p3 direction is that of SC.3 When it differs from the p2 direction, the p3 slot records pred_src PRED_SC.4

The successors at p3 are chained from the highest slot down. The successor of slot 1 is the target of B when B is taken and the fall-through of the block when it is not. The successor of slot 0 is the target of A, or the successor of slot 1. A slot redirects when it is reachable and its p3 successor differs from its p2 successor.5 Because A is not taken, slot 1 is reachable, and a reversal of B changes both successors: slot 1 and slot 0 raise the redirect together, to the same address. The FTQ accepts it, and the next request starts there.6

The first redirect from slot 1 is at cyc 110 (event 5). At cyc 109, u_bpu.u_tage.u_tage_cntrl.tage_pred_meta_p2.[1].tage_prm_comp is 0 (T0 is the provider) with tage_pred_tkn 0, so slot 1 is predicted not taken. At cyc 110, u_bpu.w_sc_hit_p3.[1] is 1 and u_bpu.w_taken_p3.[1] is 1: SC predicts B taken. bpu_slot_p3.[1].pred_src is PRED_SC. bpu_redir_p3.[1].valid and bpu_redir_p3.[0].valid are both 1, with target_pc 0x8000_001C, the target of B.

At cyc 114 (event 6), the reversal goes the other way. At cyc 113, the TAGE provider for slot 1 is T1 with CTR 3'b100, weakly taken (tage_prm_comp 1, tage_prm_ctr 3'b100). SC predicts not taken, and the redirect is to 0x8000_0028, the fall-through of the block.

docs.title: 4.3 The reversals in the run
docs.text:
The run has 9 p3 redirects, all for the block at top:

cyc Event Slot p2 direction p3 direction Target 46 3 0 not taken taken 0x8000_0014 110 5 1 not taken taken 0x8000_001C 114 6 1 taken not taken 0x8000_0028 130, 136 1 taken not taken 0x8000_0028 280 8 1 taken not taken 0x8000_0028 303, 326, 349 1 taken not taken 0x8000_0028

At cyc 46, SC reverses A, which is never taken, and the backend corrects it: tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc is 0x8000_0012 at cyc 56 (event 4).

The last backend redirect for B is at cyc 204 (event 7), with tb.bkend_ftq_redir_pc 0x8000_001A. SC reverses B four more times, at cyc 280 (event 8), 303, 326 and 349. Each replaces a wrong TAGE direction with the correct one, so no backend redirect follows. The next tb.bkend_ftq_redir_val is at cyc 358 (event 9), when the back edge falls through.

docs.title: 5. Events
docs.text: # cyc Event Other 0 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests 0x8000_0000 the same cycle fast init 1 22 first backend misprediction, the back edge; redirect to 0x8000_0008 pass 0 2 45 first p2 group for the block at top with both slots: A and B, pred_src PRED_TAGE A slot 0, B slot 1 3 46 first p3 redirect: SC reverses A in slot 0 to 0x8000_0014 4 56 A mispredicted; redirect to 0x8000_0012 backend 5 110 first p3 redirect from slot 1: SC reverses B from not taken to taken to 0x8000_001C 6 114 SC corrects TAGE's taken for B, provider T1 to 0x8000_0028 7 204 last backend misprediction of B; redirect to 0x8000_001A backend 8 280 first SC correction of B after the last backend misprediction of B no backend redirect follows 9 358 back edge falls through, a misprediction; redirect to 0x8000_0030 pass 47 10 368 the run ends

docs.title: FD-23 A Jump Behind Two Conditionals
fd23_jump_cut: A Jump Behind Two Conditionals
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd23_jump_cut (FD-23) demonstrates a prediction block with two conditional branches followed by a jump. With two prediction slots, an FTB entry holds at most two branches, so when the jump resolves, the FTB splits the entry: it keeps the two conditional branches and ends the block at the address of the jump. The next block starts at the jump and predicts it in slot 0.

The program runs a 24-pass loop whose first block holds two never-taken conditional branches, C1 and C2, followed by a jump, J.

The result line in the log file reports the blocks the FTB ends at the jump, the jumps predicted in slot 0 of the next block, and the blocks cut by the cluster.

This scenario runs in the 2-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=2.
