Item Counter Counted blocks the FTB ends at the jump n_jmp_end both slots are conditional branches predicted not taken, bpu_blk_pft_p2 is the address of J, and u_bpu.w_cut_p2 is clear the jump predicted in the next block n_jmp_next the next group whose u_bpu.r_pc_p2 is that address has a jump in slot 0, at position 0, predicted taken blocks cut by the cluster n_cut groups with u_bpu.w_cut_p2 set

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd23 in programs/fd23_jump_cut.svh.

The code consists of a short prologue, a loop of 24 passes, and a short epilogue. The first block of the loop holds C1 and C2, never taken, followed by J, a jump to a block at 0x8000_0400 that holds the back edge.

The program runs in M-mode with bare addressing.

Address      Label  Instruction              Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1             ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1             ; prologue

0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1             ; filler
0x8000_000A  C1:    bne    x6, x0, 0x8000_0010 ; never taken
0x8000_000E         c.addi a0, 1             ; always executed
0x8000_0010  C2:    bne    x6, x0, 0x8000_0016 ; never taken
0x8000_0014         c.addi a0, 1             ; always executed
0x8000_0016  J:     jal    x0, 0x8000_0400   ; the jump

0x8000_0400         c.addi a0, 1             ; filler
0x8000_0402         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; filler
0x8000_0406         bne    x6, x0, top       ; back edge, passes 0 to 22

0x8000_040A         c.addi a0, 1             ; epilogue
0x8000_040C         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; epilogue
0x8000_0410         c.addi a0, 1             ; epilogue
0x8000_0412  hold:  jal    x0, hold          ; termination

In the block at top, C1 is at halfword position 1, C2 at position 4 and J at position 7.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to place the branches.

The directions and targets are chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in them. x6 is never read.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows the block at top. Section 4.1 describes the FTB entry and the split, section 4.2 the block that ends at the jump, and section 4.3 the next block, which predicts the jump.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

The waveform group bp_cluster_p2_ftb contains the FTB fields and the block end, bp_cluster_p2 the p2 group, bp_cluster_p3 the p3 redirects, ftq the accepted groups and the predecode redirects, bp_cluster_p0 the p0 request, ftb_update the FTB updates, and backend the backend redirects.

The figure below shows the entry before and after the split, and the next block.

docs.title: 4.1 The FTB entry for top
docs.text:
The FTB keeps one entry per block start. An update for a branch resolved in a block from that start adds the branch to the entry. When the entry already holds a branch at that position, the update changes that branch in place. The entry stores its branches in position order.

An entry holds at most NUM_PRED_SLOTS branches. When an update would make it hold more, the lowest NUM_PRED_SLOTS positions are kept, the block end becomes the address of the lowest branch not kept, and a jump not kept clears the jump field. This is the split.1 The uBTB applies the same rule.2

C1 and C2 resolve first. At cyc 52 (event 3) the FTB allocates the entry for top with C1, and at cyc 53 it adds C2. The entry ends one block above its start, at 0x8000_0028. At cyc 56 (event 4), the first p2 group for top predicts both taken (TAGE's base table starts weakly taken). At cyc 57 (event 5), bpu_redir_p3.[0].valid and bpu_redir_p3.[1].valid are both 1, with target_pc 0x8000_0028: the statistical corrector reverses both at p3.

J then resolves in a block from top, and it is the third branch. At cyc 65 (event 6), ftb_upd_pc_u0 is 0x8000_0008, ftb_upd_pos_u0 is 7, ftb_upd_is_jmp_u0 is 1, and u_bpu.u_ftb.u_ftb_cntrl.upd_split is 1 with upd_cut_pos 7. The entry keeps C1 and C2, and now ends at position 7, the address of J.

The first upd_split of the run is at cyc 41, for the same reason. On the first pass, the block from the reset vector holds C1, C2 and J at positions 5, 8 and 11.

docs.title: 4.2 The block ends at the jump
docs.text:
At p2, the cluster places each conditional field of the entry in its slot, and the jump field in the lowest slot that holds no conditional branch.3 The entry for top has no jump field, so the two slots hold C1 and C2. The fall-through of the block, the address fetch continues at when no slot is taken, is the stored end of the FTB entry when the FTB answers, no branch is cut and no jump is held.4 It leaves the cluster as bpu_blk_pft_p2. The cut, which would end the block at a branch the FTB reports and no slot carries, stays clear.5

The first accepted p2 group of the block at top that ends at J is at cyc 71 (event 7). u_bpu.r_pc_p2 is 0x8000_0008. u_bpu.w_ftb_br_valid_p2.[0] and u_bpu.w_ftb_br_valid_p2.[1] are 1, u_bpu.w_ftb_jmp_valid_p2 is 0, u_bpu.w_cut_p2 is 0, and bpu_blk_pft_p2 is 0x8000_0016, the address of J. bpu_slot_p2.[0] is C1 and bpu_slot_p2.[1] is C2, both COND at pos 1 and 4, not taken, pred_src PRED_TAGE.

The uBTB was split the same way. Its p1 prediction for top, bpu_pred_pft_p1, is 0x8000_0016 from cyc 70, so p1 and p2 agree.

docs.title: 4.3 The next block predicts the jump
docs.text:
The next block starts at 0x8000_0016. The predictors have not seen this block start, so at first neither the uBTB nor the FTB answers for it. Fetch runs past J, and predecode at F3 finds it: u_ftq.w_pd_redir_pc is 0x8000_0400 at cyc 79 and 92. The update for J from that start allocates its entry at cyc 91 (event 8), with J at position 0. From then on, the FTB answers for 0x8000_0016 with J in its jump field, and the cluster places J in slot 0.

The first counted pair is at cyc 97 and 98. At cyc 97, the block at top ends at 0x8000_0016, as in section 4.2. At cyc 98 (event 9), u_bpu.r_pc_p2 is 0x8000_0016 and bpu_slot_p2.[0] is DIRECT_UNC at pos 0, taken, with target 0x8000_0400 and pred_src PRED_FTB.

The blocks at cyc 71 and 84 ended at J before the entry for J existed, and their next groups had no FTB answer. The count of blocks that end at J, 23, therefore exceeds the count of next blocks, 21.

docs.title: 5. Events
docs.text: # cyc Event Other 0 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests 0x8000_0000 the same cycle fast init 1 19 predecode redirect to 0x8000_0400: J found at F3, not yet known to the predictors pass 0 2 41 first backend misprediction, the back edge; redirect to 0x8000_0008 pass 0 3 52 FTB entry for top allocated with C1; C2 added at cyc 53 ftb_update 4 56 first p2 group for top: C1 and C2 in slots 0 and 1, end 0x8000_0028 predicted taken 5 57 SC reverses both at p3; redirect to 0x8000_0028 p3 redirect 6 65 J resolved from top: the split, upd_split 1, the entry ends at 0x8000_0016 upd_cut_pos 7 7 71 first p2 group for top ending at 0x8000_0016, C1 and C2 not taken, w_cut_p2 0 counted, n_jmp_end 8 91 FTB entry for 0x8000_0016 allocated with J at position 0 ftb_update 9 98 the block at 0x8000_0016 predicts J in slot 0, taken, to 0x8000_0400 counted, n_jmp_next 10 234 back edge falls through, a misprediction; redirect to 0x8000_040A pass 23 11 244 the run ends

docs.title: fd24_call_slot1: A Call in Slot 1
docs.text:
Open waveform

Runs Surfer in the browser, with nothing to install. The signal setup takes a few seconds to apply.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
fd24_call_slot1 (FD-24) demonstrates a call in slot 1. A prediction block holds a conditional branch followed by a call, so the conditional branch is in slot 0 and the call in slot 1. When the conditional branch is predicted not taken, the call is on the predicted path, and the return address stack (RAS) pushes its return address at p2. The return from the function is then predicted from the stack.

The program runs a 24-pass loop whose first block holds C, a never-taken conditional branch, followed by a call to a function, f.

The result line in the log file reports the RAS pushes from slot 1 and the returns predicted by the RAS.

This scenario runs in the 2-prediction slot Pacino configuration, NUM_PRED_SLOTS=2.

Item Counter Counted RAS pushes from slot 1 n_push_s1 p2 groups accepted by the FTQ, u_ftq.w_ok_slot_p2, with slot 0 a conditional branch predicted not taken and slot 1 a call presented to the RAS returns predicted by the RAS n_ras_ret_ok retired returns whose slot has pred_src PRED_RAS and the correct target

docs.title: 3. The program
docs.text:
The program is written by the task prog_fd24 in programs/fd24_call_slot1.svh.

The code consists of a short prologue, a loop of 24 passes, and a short epilogue. The first block of the loop holds C, never taken, followed by a call to f. The function returns to the block that holds the back edge.

The program runs in M-mode with bare addressing.

Address      Label  Instruction              Purpose
0x8000_0000         c.addi a0, 1             ; prologue
0x8000_0002         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; prologue
0x8000_0006         c.addi a0, 1             ; prologue

0x8000_0008  top:   c.addi a0, 1             ; filler
0x8000_000A  C:     bne    x6, x0, 0x8000_0010 ; never taken
0x8000_000E         c.addi a0, 1             ; always executed
0x8000_0010         jal    x1, f             ; the call
0x8000_0014         c.addi a0, 1             ; return address
0x8000_0016         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; filler
0x8000_001A         bne    x6, x0, top       ; back edge, passes 0 to 22

0x8000_001E         c.addi a0, 1             ; epilogue
0x8000_0020         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; epilogue
0x8000_0024         c.addi a0, 1             ; epilogue
0x8000_0026  hold:  jal    x0, hold          ; termination

0x8000_0400  f:     c.addi a0, 1             ; function body
0x8000_0402         addi   t0, t0, 1         ; function body
0x8000_0406         ret                      ; return to 0x8000_0014

In the block at top, C is at halfword position 1 and the call at position 4.

The c.addi and addi instructions do no useful work. Their purpose is to mix 16-bit and 32-bit instructions and to place the branches.

The directions and targets are chosen by the program writer and resolved by the modeled backend, and the register operands play no part in them. x6 is never read.

docs.title: 4. Walkthrough
docs.text:
The walkthrough follows the call and its return. Section 4.1 describes how the call reaches slot 1, section 4.2 the RAS push, and section 4.3 the return predicted from the stack.

Cycle numbers below are events in section 5; each event is a marker in the waveform.

The waveform group bp_cluster_p2 contains the p2 group, ras the speculative stack, ftq the accepted groups and the predecode redirects, ras_commit the commit stack, and backend the backend redirects.

The figure below shows the block, the push and the return.

docs.title: 4.1 The call reaches slot 1
docs.text: The FTB entry for the block at top holds C in its first conditional field and the call in its jump field. At p2, the cluster places C in slot 0. The call goes to the lowest slot that holds no conditional branch, which is slot 1.1 A taken branch ends the block, so a slot is on the predicted path only when no earlier slot is predicted taken.2

docs.title: 4.2 The RAS operation of slot 1
docs.text:
At p2, a slot of a valid block is presented to the RAS when it holds a branch on the predicted path.3 The RAS performs the operations of the slots in order, slot 0 first, so a call in slot 1 pushes its return address after the operation of slot 0.4 A push allocates an entry at the write pointer, TOSW, and the read pointer, TOSR, moves to it.5

The first counted push is at cyc 90 (event 5). It is also the first p2 group for top with both slots valid. u_bpu.r_pc_p2 is 0x8000_0008. bpu_slot_p2.[0] is C, a COND at pos 1, not taken, pred_src PRED_TAGE. bpu_slot_p2.[1] is the call, DIRECT_CALL at pos 4, taken, with target 0x8000_0400 and pred_src PRED_FTB. u_bpu.w_ras_pred_val_p2.[1] is 1 with u_bpu.w_br_type_p2.[1] DIRECT_CALL. u_bpu.w_ras_pred_val_p2.[0] is 1 for C, a conditional branch, on which the RAS does not act.

At cyc 91 (event 6), u_bpu.u_ras.tosr has moved from 0 to 1 and u_bpu.u_ras.tosw from 0 to 2. u_bpu.u_ras.spec_ret_addr.[1] holds 0x8000_0014, the return address of the call.

docs.title: 4.3 The return predicted from the stack
docs.text:
The block at f holds the return. At p2, a return slot takes the RAS pop address as its target when the pop is valid, with pred_src PRED_RAS.6 Of the 25 accepted p2 groups for the block at 0x8000_0400, 23 predict the return from the RAS with target 0x8000_0014. The first is at cyc 91 (event 6), the cycle after the first counted push. The log count, 21, is of retired returns.

Before cyc 90, predecode finds the call four times, each time in a block whose start has no FTB entry holding it yet. Each block start has its own entry. u_ftq.w_pd_redir_pc is 0x8000_0400 at these cycles:

cyc Event Block start Reached by 19 1 0x8000_0000 pass 0 60 0x8000_0008 the first backend redirect of the back edge 75 0x8000_0010 the target of C, while C is predicted taken 85 0x8000_000E the fall-through of C, after the backend corrects C

The commit stack follows when the call and the return retire, behind the speculative pointers. u_bpu.u_ras.csp is 1 at cyc 98 (event 7), with u_bpu.u_ras.tosw already at 3. The run has 48 RAS commits, ras_commit_val: a push and a pop for each of the 24 passes.

docs.title: 5. Events
docs.text: # cyc Event Other 0 0 reset released (tb.rstn); the FTQ requests 0x8000_0000 the same cycle fast init 1 19 predecode redirect to 0x8000_0400: the call found at F3, not yet known to the predictors pass 0 2 40 first return mispredicted, cold; redirect to 0x8000_0014 backend 3 51 back edge mispredicted, cold; redirect to 0x8000_0008 backend 4 76 C mispredicted taken; redirect to 0x8000_000E backend 5 90 first RAS push from slot 1, behind C not taken; the first p2 group for top with both slots counted 6 91 TOSR 1, TOSW 2; entry 1 holds 0x8000_0014; first return predicted from the RAS PRED_RAS 7 98 the next call commits: u_ras.csp 1 speculative pointers ahead 8 261 back edge falls through, a misprediction; redirect to 0x8000_001E pass 23 9 270 the run ends

docs.title: fe_top Connectivity Inventory
docs.text:
This file records the net-level connectivity of fe_top. The block diagrams docs/fe_block.svg and docs/fe_pipe.svg use it as the reference for connections between blocks.

Section 3 lists the nets between instances, section 4 lists the fe_top boundary ports, section 6 lists the predictors inside bp_cluster, and section 7 describes the page table walker that the testbench places beside fe_top.

docs.title: 1. Notation
docs.text:
Notation:

  • W bits is the packed width. N x W bits is an unpacked array of N elements, each W bits wide.
  • from is the instance output that drives a net, and to is the instance input that reads it.
  • bind fe_top.sv:L is the line of the port connection.
  • A file name without a directory is one of the module files listed in section 2.1.

fe_top is a purely structural module containing 7 instances, 141 nets between instances (section 3) and 75 top-level ports (section 4).

4. The fe_top boundary
docs.text:
The ports are declared at fe_top.sv:96-217 and grouped as FE-17 (planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1378) and FE-20 (planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1445) group them; fe_top.sv:29-60 restates the grouping. -> is a fe_top input read by an instance input; <- is a fe_top output driven by an instance output.

FE-17 counts two groups that cross (translation and backend) and says the instruction path is not a boundary group: what crosses is the L1I's l2-side port mem, a topology edge. FE-20 adds three inward groups (csr, config, maintenance) and one outward dependency, the ibuf read ready. The RTL carries all of them as fe_top ports; the L1I's mem port is section 4.8. Two outputs are in no group (section 4.12).

bkend_ftq_redir_val is the one fe_top net with two readers: the FTQ and the ibuf clear (fe_top.sv:44-45, IBUF-13).

docs.title: 6. Inside bp_cluster
docs.text: The cluster is a four-stage pipeline (p0 to p3) with an update stage u0 and its write u1 (bp_cluster.sv:55-61). The FTQ-facing ports are grouped in the port list as follows; the predictor instances are at bp_cluster.sv:1812-2035.

docs.title: 6.1 bp_cluster port groups
docs.text:
group                                       ports at       spec
P0  prediction request, FTQ -> BPU          bp_cluster.sv:109-112
                                            ftq_bpu 3
P1  initial prediction, BPU -> FTQ          :114-123   ftq_bpu 4
RD  redirects p2, p3                        :125-131   ftq_bpu 6
SL  slot correction p2, p3                  :133-150   ftq_bpu 4a
BK  block-scalar correction p2              :152-160   ftq_bpu 4c

M3  metadata write p3 (sc)                  :177-182   ftq_bpu 7.2
UP  updates u0: ubtb lp ftb tage ittage sc  :184-224   ftq_bpu 8

RB  history rollback                        :236-263   ftq_bpu 9
HI  history pointer and buffer outputs      :265-271   ftq_bpu 9

                                       the tb nets of lines 27-99
ptw u_ptw (.*)      fe_tb_dut.svh:122  rtl/mmu/ptw/rtl/ptw.sv:155

What connects them, all by .* name matching:

The walker and the L1I read one memory image (fe_tb_mem.svh; FE-21, planning/arch/fe_decisions.md:1490, ptw_mem_interfaces.md WM-10, line 143). fe_csr and ptw_csr are packed from the one csr_tb_pkg shadow (fe_tb_dut.svh:119-121).

docs.title: 8. Disagreements between the RTL and the planning documents
docs.text:
The RTL is what sections 2 to 7 record.

D1  FTB update port count.
    RTL: 15 payload ports plus the valid (fe_top.sv:274-289;
    bp_cluster.sv:195-211). The comments fe_top.sv:69, fe_top.sv:273,
    bp_cluster.sv:194 and ftq.sv:200 say 14.
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8 says 15 (lines 883, 895-900; "This
    read 14"). The plan agrees with the ports; the four RTL comments
    are stale since BP-121 added ftb_upd_jmp_rvc_u0.

D2  ITTAGE update payload name.
    RTL: ittage_upd_inp_u0 (fe_top.sv:298; bp_cluster.sv:219-220;
    ftq port bound at fe_top.sv:568).
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8 table, line 885, "ittage_upd_inp".

D3  TAGE and ITTAGE queue status port names (TD#49).
    RTL: tage.sv:47-48 and ittage.sv:46-47 declare <p>_pq_not_full and
    <p>_uq_not_full; bp_cluster.sv:1945-1946 and 1968-1969 bind them;
    bp_cluster.sv:286-288 says TD#49 was applied by BP-132.
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8, lines 947-956, says tage and
    ittage declare pq_not_full and upd_rdy without prefix and that
    TD#49 is not yet applied. The cluster boundary names (tage_upd_rdy,
    ittage_upd_rdy) agree with lines 938-939.

D4  uBTB update port at the cluster boundary.
    RTL: ubtb_upd_u0, ubtb_upd_t [NUM_PRED_SLOTS-1:0], 352 bits
    (bp_cluster.sv:186; fe_top.sv:292).
    Plan: ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 8 (line 881) names only the predictor
    port upd_u0; no planning document names the boundary port.

D5  Observation outputs.
    RTL: ftq_full and ftq_empty are fe_top outputs (fe_top.sv:212-216).
    Plan: in no FE-17 or FE-20 group (fe_decisions.md:1378, 1445) and
    named by no interface document.

D6  Decode outputs.
    RTL: decode_bundle, vec_decode_bundle, is_vector, pd_out,
    vtype_hazard (fe_top.sv:103-107), from u_dec (fe_top.sv:820-824).
    Plan: FE-17 backend (fe_decisions.md:1410) says "decode to rename
    and dispatch" with no port list; no interface document names
    decode_bundle, vec_decode_bundle or pd_out (is_vector and
    vtype_hazard appear in dcd_decisions.md:612 and 262).

D7  The instruction group.
    RTL: fe_top.sv:30-32 lists "instruction" as a boundary group, the
    20 l1i_mem_* ports (fe_top.sv:167-186).
    Plan: FE-17 (fe_decisions.md:1378, 1385) counts two groups and
